title: Swift Quick Start: Swift + SwiftUI + UIKit (en,it)
details:
Micro-modules for Swift, SwiftUI, and UIKit.
Cards are rule-based: Rule + Takeaway + Trap.
No practice/exercises inside modules.

modules.title: 1. Swift Basics
modules.moduleDescription: Swift fundamentals: variables/constants, types, strings, numbers, operators, tuples, ranges, and console output.

cards.title: let vs var
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `let` for constants and `var` for variables.
Takeaway: Default to `let`, switch to `var` only if the value must change.
Trap: A `let` struct instance can’t mutate any stored properties.

cards.title: Type inference
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift infers types from the assigned value.
Takeaway: `let x = 5` is `Int` without writing `: Int`.
Trap: `1` is `Int`, `1.0` is `Double`—don’t mix them silently.

cards.title: Explicit type annotation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can annotate types: `let pi: Double = 3.14`.
Takeaway: Use annotations when inference is unclear or for readability.
Trap: Over-annotating everywhere adds noise.

cards.title: Printing values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `print()` for quick debugging output.
Takeaway: `print(value)` is the fastest sanity check.
Trap: Don’t ship production logic that depends on print statements.

cards.title: String interpolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Embed values with `\(value)` inside strings.
Takeaway: `"Hello, \(name)"` is clearer than concatenation.
Trap: Interpolation is not formatting—control decimals explicitly if needed.

cards.title: String concatenation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Combine strings with `+` or interpolation.
Takeaway: Prefer interpolation for readability.
Trap: `+` chains can get slow/ugly in large builds of text.

cards.title: Multiline strings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use triple quotes `"""` for multiline strings.
Takeaway: Great for templates and JSON snippets.
Trap: Indentation becomes part of the string if you’re not careful.

cards.title: Escaping characters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Escape quotes and backslashes: `\"`, `\\`.
Takeaway: Makes literal strings valid Swift.
Trap: Mis-escaping leads to compile errors or unexpected output.

cards.title: Unicode in strings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift strings are Unicode-correct.
Takeaway: Emojis count as characters, not bytes.
Trap: String indexing isn’t integer-based—don’t assume `s[0]`.

cards.title: String indices
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Index strings with `String.Index`, not Int.
Takeaway: Use `s.startIndex`, `s.index(after:)`.
Trap: Converting to `[Character]` is easy but may be costly.

cards.title: String value semantics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `String` is a value type with copy-on-write.
Takeaway: Copies are cheap until you mutate.
Trap: Don’t fear passing strings around.

cards.title: Int vs Double
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Int` is whole numbers, `Double` is floating-point.
Takeaway: Pick based on domain (money often needs Decimal).
Trap: Mixing `Int` and `Double` requires explicit conversion.

cards.title: Type conversion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convert explicitly: `Double(x)` or `Int(d)`.
Takeaway: Swift avoids implicit numeric conversions.
Trap: `Int(3.9)` truncates to `3`—it does not round.

cards.title: Integer division
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Int / Int` performs integer division.
Takeaway: `5/2 == 2`.
Trap: Expecting `2.5`—use `Double(5)/2`.

cards.title: Remainder operator %
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `%` returns the remainder of integer division.
Takeaway: Useful for parity and wrapping.
Trap: Negative values can surprise—test your edge cases.

cards.title: Booleans only
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Conditions must be `Bool` in Swift.
Takeaway: No truthy/falsy—`if 1 {}` won’t compile.
Trap: Comparing with `== true` is usually redundant.

cards.title: Comparison operators
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.
Takeaway: Keep comparisons simple and readable.
Trap: Don’t compare floating-point for exact equality unless you mean it.

cards.title: Logical operators
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `&&`, `||`, and `!`.
Takeaway: Short-circuiting can avoid crashes (e.g., nil checks).
Trap: Parentheses help readability when conditions get complex.

cards.title: Ternary operator
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `condition ? a : b` picks one of two values.
Takeaway: Great for simple decisions.
Trap: Nested ternaries hurt readability—use `if` instead.

cards.title: Optionals exist
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `T?` means a value can be missing (`nil`).
Takeaway: Swift forces you to handle absence safely.
Trap: `nil` is not `0` and not `""`.

cards.title: Swift Basics — Nil-coalescing ??
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `optional ?? fallback` provides a default.
Takeaway: One-liner fallback for optionals.
Trap: It resolves one optional level; `T??` needs extra handling.

cards.title: ?? precedence
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `??` has lower precedence than `+` and many others.
Takeaway: Add parentheses when mixing: `(a ?? 0) + 1`.
Trap: Without parentheses you may get a compile error or wrong logic.

cards.title: Swift Basics — Force unwrap !
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid `optional!` unless you’re 100% sure.
Takeaway: Prefer `if let` / `guard let`.
Trap: `!` crashes at runtime when nil appears.

cards.title: Swift Basics — if let unwrap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if let x = opt { ... }` safely unwraps.
Takeaway: Inside the block `x` is non-optional.
Trap: `x` only exists inside that scope.

cards.title: Swift Basics — guard let unwrap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let x = opt else { return }`.
Takeaway: Early exit keeps code flat.
Trap: `guard` must exit the scope (return/throw/break).

cards.title: Closed ranges
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `1...5` includes 5.
Takeaway: Use for inclusive loops.
Trap: Off-by-one errors come from using the wrong range type.

cards.title: Half-open ranges
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `0..<count` excludes `count`.
Takeaway: Perfect for indexing arrays.
Trap: `0...count` is usually wrong (out of bounds).

cards.title: Range contains
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check membership with `range.contains(x)`.
Takeaway: Clear and readable.
Trap: Don’t manually do `x>=a && x<=b` unless needed.

cards.title: Tuples basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tuples group values: `(Int, String)`.
Takeaway: Great for returning two values quickly.
Trap: For complex data, prefer a struct.

cards.title: Named tuples
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Name tuple elements: `(min: 1, max: 10)`.
Takeaway: Better readability.
Trap: Tuples don’t scale—too many fields becomes messy.

cards.title: Tuple destructuring
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unpack: `let (a,b) = pair`.
Takeaway: Cleaner than `pair.0` / `pair.1`.
Trap: Keep names meaningful; avoid `a,b,c` soup.

cards.title: Swap with tuples
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swap values: `(a,b) = (b,a)`.
Takeaway: Simple and safe.
Trap: Prefer `swap(&a, &b)` when clarity matters.

cards.title: Compound assignment
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`.
Takeaway: Shorter updates.
Trap: Integer division rules still apply.

cards.title: Operator precedence
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Learn precedence (or add parentheses).
Takeaway: Parentheses beat guessing.
Trap: Reading precedence tables mid-debug is pain—write clear code.

cards.title: Semicolons
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Semicolons are optional in Swift.
Takeaway: Use new lines instead.
Trap: Two statements on one line hides bugs.

cards.title: Comments
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `//` for single-line, `/* ... */` for blocks.
Takeaway: Explain why, not what.
Trap: Outdated comments mislead.

cards.title: Naming conventions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use lowerCamelCase for variables/functions.
Takeaway: `userName`, not `User_Name`.
Trap: Bad names become bugs.

cards.title: Reserved keywords
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Escape keywords with backticks: ``let `class` = 1``.
Takeaway: Helpful when mapping weird keys.
Trap: Overusing backticks hurts readability.

cards.title: Array literals
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Arrays use `[1,2,3]` and type `[T]`.
Takeaway: Type is inferred from elements.
Trap: `[]` needs a type context.

cards.title: Empty arrays
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `var a: [Int] = []` for empty arrays.
Takeaway: Declare the type.
Trap: `let a = []` won’t compile.

cards.title: Dictionary literals
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dictionaries use `["a": 1]` and type `[K:V]`.
Takeaway: Keys are unique.
Trap: Lookup returns an optional.

cards.title: Empty dictionaries
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `var d: [String:Int] = [:]`.
Takeaway: Use `[:]` for empty dictionary literals.
Trap: `[]` is an empty array literal, not a dictionary.

cards.title: Set literals
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Set` can be created from an array literal with a type context.
Takeaway: `let s: Set<Int> = [1,2,3]`.
Trap: `[1,2]` is an Array unless typed as Set.

cards.title: isEmpty vs count
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `isEmpty` to `count == 0`.
Takeaway: Clear intent.
Trap: Some collections compute count more expensively.

cards.title: Dictionary default value
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key, default: 0]` provides a default.
Takeaway: Great for counters.
Trap: It mutates the dictionary—needs `var`.

cards.title: Set order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sets do not preserve order.
Takeaway: Convert to array and sort for UI.
Trap: “Looks ordered” is accidental.

cards.title: Type inspection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `type(of:)` to inspect inferred types.
Takeaway: Helps debug inference.
Trap: Don’t build real logic on runtime type checks.

cards.title: Safe casting as?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `as?` for safe casting.
Takeaway: Returns nil if the cast fails.
Trap: Handle nil explicitly to avoid silent failures.

cards.title: Forced casting as!
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid `as!` unless guaranteed.
Takeaway: Prefer `as?` + unwrap.
Trap: `as!` crashes if the type is unexpected.

cards.title: Type check is
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `is` to check a type.
Takeaway: Useful for debugging.
Trap: Heavy `Any` usage is a design smell.

cards.title: NaN check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NaN is not equal to itself.
Takeaway: Use `isNaN`.
Trap: `nan == nan` is false.

cards.title: Float equality tolerance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compare Doubles with an epsilon.
Takeaway: `abs(a-b) < eps`.
Trap: Exact equality often fails.

cards.title: Numeric underscores
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use underscores for readability: `1_000_000`.
Takeaway: Same value, clearer.
Trap: Don’t make them confusing.

cards.title: Binary/hex literals
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `0b` and `0x` for bit work.
Takeaway: Helpful for masks.
Trap: Document your intent to avoid confusion.

cards.title: Bitwise vs logical
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `& | ^ << >>` are bitwise; `&& || !` are logical.
Takeaway: Different domains.
Trap: Mixing them is a classic bug.

cards.title: Overflow operators
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `&+ &- &*` wrap on overflow.
Takeaway: Use when wrapping is intended.
Trap: Normal `+` may trap in debug on overflow.

cards.title: Int.min trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `-Int.min` overflows.
Takeaway: Handle extremes carefully.
Trap: Can crash in debug or produce wrapped results.

cards.title: String prefix/suffix
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `hasPrefix` / `hasSuffix`.
Takeaway: Cleaner than manual slicing.
Trap: Case sensitivity matters for user input.

cards.title: Case-sensitive compare
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `==` is case-sensitive.
Takeaway: Normalize if needed.
Trap: Locale-sensitive compare needs specialized APIs.

cards.title: UpperCamelCase types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Type names use UpperCamelCase.
Takeaway: `UserProfile`.
Trap: Inconsistent naming hurts Xcode search/autocomplete.

cards.title: Avoid magic numbers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use named constants for meaning.
Takeaway: `let maxRetries = 3`.
Trap: Don’t create constants for every trivial value.

cards.title: Minimal imports
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Import only what you need.
Takeaway: Add Foundation when required.
Trap: Missing imports cause confusing errors—add when APIs demand it.

cards.title: Scope basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep variables scoped as small as possible.
Takeaway: Less state, fewer bugs.
Trap: Reusing names across scopes confuses code.

cards.title: Shadowing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid shadowing important names.
Takeaway: Use clear new names.
Trap: Shadowing hides optional unwrap mistakes.

cards.title: Constant initialization
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Constants can be initialized from expressions/functions.
Takeaway: `let id = UUID()`.
Trap: If it needs to change later, it must be `var`.

cards.title: Unary minus
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unary `-` negates numbers.
Takeaway: `-x`.
Trap: Watch overflow at extremes.

cards.title: String to Int
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Int("123")` returns `Int?`.
Takeaway: Always unwrap.
Trap: Trim spaces for user input.

cards.title: Printing Bool
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `print(flag)` prints `true/false`.
Takeaway: Simple debug.
Trap: Don’t log secrets.

cards.title: Swift Basics — Parameter labels
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Parameter labels make call sites readable.
Takeaway: `move(from:to:)`.
Trap: Bad labels make APIs painful.

cards.title: Doc comments
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `///` shows in Quick Help.
Takeaway: Document public APIs.
Trap: Stale docs mislead.

cards.title: Code formatting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Consistent formatting reduces cognitive load.
Takeaway: Use a formatter (SwiftFormat) if possible.
Trap: Style debates waste time—automate.

cards.title: Playground basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Playgrounds are great for quick experiments.
Takeaway: Test syntax and small ideas fast.
Trap: Behavior can differ from app runtime.

cards.title: Strong typing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift is strongly typed.
Takeaway: Safer code and better tooling.
Trap: Overusing `Any` throws away the benefit.

cards.title: Optional comparison
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Optionals compare only when the wrapped type supports it.
Takeaway: Be explicit for clarity.
Trap: Nil ordering surprises—avoid clever comparisons.

cards.title: Swift Basics — Dictionary lookup optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key]` returns `Value?`.
Takeaway: Missing keys are normal.
Trap: Force-unwrapping dict lookups is a common crash.

cards.title: Set uniqueness
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set stores unique elements.
Takeaway: Great for membership checks.
Trap: Don’t use Set when ordering matters.

cards.title: Refactor let-first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `let` until mutation is required.
Takeaway: Less accidental state.
Trap: Premature `var` invites bugs.

cards.title: Readability > cleverness
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Write code for humans first.
Takeaway: Clear names + small expressions.
Trap: Clever one-liners become debugging debt.

modules.title: 2. Control Flow
modules.moduleDescription: If/guard/switch, loops, pattern matching basics, and writing clear branching logic.

cards.title: if basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if` requires a `Bool` condition.
Takeaway: Use `if condition { ... }` (no parentheses needed).
Trap: Swift has no truthy/falsy—only `Bool` works.

cards.title: else if chain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `else if` for multiple conditions.
Takeaway: Order conditions from most specific to most general.
Trap: Overlong chains are a smell—consider `switch`.

cards.title: guard basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard` enforces a condition and exits early if it fails.
Takeaway: Prefer `guard` to reduce nesting.
Trap: `guard` must exit the scope (`return/throw/break/continue`).

cards.title: Control Flow — guard let unwrap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let x = opt else { return }` safely unwraps optionals.
Takeaway: After the guard, `x` is non-optional.
Trap: Don’t use `!` when a guard fits.

cards.title: switch is exhaustive
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `switch` must cover all cases.
Takeaway: Handle all `enum` cases (or provide `default`).
Trap: A `default` can hide missing cases when enums evolve.

cards.title: switch with ranges
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `switch` can match ranges and patterns.
Takeaway: Great for score bands (`0..<50`, `50..<80`, etc.).
Trap: Watch half-open vs closed ranges to avoid off-by-one.

cards.title: switch where
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Add `where` to refine a case.
Takeaway: `case let x where x.isMultiple(of: 2):`.
Trap: Too many `where` clauses can hurt readability.

cards.title: fallthrough
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `fallthrough` forces execution to continue to the next case.
Takeaway: Rarely needed—use explicit logic instead.
Trap: `fallthrough` does not re-check pattern conditions.

cards.title: for-in array
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `for x in array { ... }` to iterate.
Takeaway: Simple and safe iteration.
Trap: Don’t mutate the array structure while iterating.

cards.title: for-in dictionary
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Iterate dictionaries with `for (k, v) in dict`.
Takeaway: You get key and value at once.
Trap: Dictionary iteration order is not guaranteed.

cards.title: for-in set
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Iterate sets with `for x in set`.
Takeaway: Use Set for membership, not order.
Trap: Don’t assume a stable order.

cards.title: indices vs 0..<count
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `array.indices` over `0..<array.count`.
Takeaway: Safer with slices and custom collections.
Trap: `0..<count` is fine for arrays, but not universal.

cards.title: Control Flow — enumerated()
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `enumerated()` to get index and value.
Takeaway: `for (i, x) in arr.enumerated()`.
Trap: `i` is an Int offset, not a collection Index for all collections.

cards.title: stride loops
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `stride(from:to:by:)` or `stride(from:through:by:)`.
Takeaway: Avoid manual index math.
Trap: `to:` excludes the end; `through:` includes it.

cards.title: while basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `while condition { ... }` repeats while true.
Takeaway: Use when the end condition is unknown.
Trap: Forgetting to update state causes infinite loops.

cards.title: repeat-while basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `repeat { ... } while condition` runs at least once.
Takeaway: Good for “do first, then check”.
Trap: Condition is checked after the body, not before.

cards.title: break
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `break` exits a loop or switch.
Takeaway: Use to stop early when you found what you need.
Trap: Too many breaks can make flow hard to follow.

cards.title: continue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `continue` skips to the next loop iteration.
Takeaway: Great for filtering early.
Trap: Overusing continue can hide important logic.

cards.title: nested loops
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nested loops multiply work.
Takeaway: Be mindful of performance (O(n²) happens fast).
Trap: Large nested loops on the main thread cause UI jank.

cards.title: labeled statements
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use labels to break/continue outer loops.
Takeaway: `outer: for ... { for ... { break outer } }`.
Trap: Labels can reduce clarity—use sparingly.

cards.title: pattern matching in if
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if case` can match patterns.
Takeaway: `if case .loaded(let d) = state { ... }`.
Trap: If it gets complex, switch is clearer.

cards.title: Control Flow — guard case
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard case` combines pattern match + early exit.
Takeaway: Keeps code flat.
Trap: Don’t cram many conditions into one guard—split if needed.

cards.title: optional binding + condition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if let x = opt, x > 0 { ... }`.
Takeaway: Unwrap and validate in one line.
Trap: Keep it readable; long conditions belong in helpers.

cards.title: switch on tuples
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `switch (a, b)` matches combinations.
Takeaway: Useful for coordinate logic.
Trap: Too many tuple cases becomes unmaintainable.

cards.title: ternary vs if
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use ternary only for simple expressions.
Takeaway: If it’s more than one line, use `if`.
Trap: Nested ternaries are a readability killer.

cards.title: short-circuit safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `&&` and `||` short-circuit.
Takeaway: Put the safest/cheapest check first.
Trap: Don’t rely on side effects in conditions.

cards.title: defer basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `defer` runs when leaving the current scope.
Takeaway: Great for cleanup.
Trap: Multiple `defer` blocks run in LIFO order.

cards.title: early returns
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Return early to avoid deep nesting.
Takeaway: Flat code is easier to maintain.
Trap: Don’t overdo it—too many early returns can fragment logic.

cards.title: guard for preconditions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use guard for required inputs.
Takeaway: Validate once at the top.
Trap: Mixing validation and business logic in one guard block.

cards.title: switch vs dictionary lookup
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use switch when there are few known cases.
Takeaway: For many mappings, consider a dictionary.
Trap: Don’t use switch as a giant lookup table.

cards.title: forEach vs for-in
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `forEach` is not a drop-in replacement for `for`.
Takeaway: `break`/`continue` don’t work inside `forEach`.
Trap: Using `return` inside `forEach` only returns from the closure.

cards.title: map is not looping for side effects
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `map` for transforms, not side effects.
Takeaway: Use `for` when you need side effects.
Trap: `map { print($0) }` is a code smell.

cards.title: filter basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `filter` keeps elements matching a predicate.
Takeaway: It returns a new collection.
Trap: Filtering large arrays repeatedly can be expensive.

cards.title: reduce basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `reduce` folds a collection into one value.
Takeaway: Great for sums and building dictionaries.
Trap: A wrong initial accumulator breaks results.

cards.title: flatMap vs compactMap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `compactMap` removes nils; `flatMap` flattens sequences.
Takeaway: Pick the correct one.
Trap: Mixing them up creates type confusion.

cards.title: guard in loops
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can use `guard` inside loops.
Takeaway: Skip invalid items with `guard ... else { continue }`.
Trap: Remember `continue` vs `return` changes scope.

cards.title: switch on enums
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer enums + switch for state.
Takeaway: The compiler forces exhaustive handling.
Trap: Using multiple booleans creates impossible states.

cards.title: multiple booleans trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Replace `isLoading/isError/hasData` combos with an enum.
Takeaway: `enum ScreenState { ... }` is safer.
Trap: Booleans produce many invalid combinations.

cards.title: looping until condition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use while/repeat-while for “unknown count” loops.
Takeaway: Keep the stop condition visible.
Trap: Hidden stop conditions lead to infinite loops.

cards.title: range-based loops
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use ranges for numeric loops.
Takeaway: `for i in 0..<n`.
Trap: Use `..<` for indices, not `...`.

cards.title: closed range pitfalls
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `0...array.count` is almost always wrong.
Takeaway: Use `0..<array.count`.
Trap: The last index is `count-1`.

cards.title: switch default usage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid `default` on enums when possible.
Takeaway: You’ll get compiler errors when new cases appear.
Trap: `default` hides missing-case bugs.

cards.title: switch value binding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Bind values in cases: `case let .some(x)`.
Takeaway: Clean extraction.
Trap: Rebinding names can shadow variables unexpectedly.

cards.title: case let shorthand
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can write `case let .some(x):`.
Takeaway: Consistent style improves readability.
Trap: Inconsistent patterns make switches hard to scan.

cards.title: where with tuples
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `where` to refine tuple matches.
Takeaway: Expressive matching.
Trap: Too clever matching reduces maintainability.

cards.title: continue with guard
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inside loops, prefer `guard ... else { continue }`.
Takeaway: Keeps happy-path aligned left.
Trap: Don’t do heavy work in the else block.

cards.title: break with label
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `break label` to exit outer loops.
Takeaway: Avoid manual flags.
Trap: Overuse labels makes control flow hard to read.

cards.title: switch vs if performance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Choose based on clarity first.
Takeaway: Modern compilers optimize both well.
Trap: Micro-optimizing branching usually wastes time.

cards.title: boolean toggling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Toggle with `flag.toggle()`.
Takeaway: Clearer than `flag = !flag`.
Trap: Don’t toggle when you actually need to set a specific state.

cards.title: guard for casting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let x = value as? Type else { return }`.
Takeaway: Safe downcasting pattern.
Trap: `as!` turns a bad cast into a crash.

cards.title: looping over characters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Iterate strings with `for ch in str`.
Takeaway: Unicode-safe.
Trap: Don’t assume each character is one byte.

cards.title: switch on characters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Switch can match characters.
Takeaway: Useful for parsing.
Trap: Use `default` carefully; whitespace/newlines matter.

cards.title: parsing with state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For complex parsing, use a state machine (enum).
Takeaway: Cleaner than nested ifs.
Trap: Ad-hoc parsing grows bugs fast.

cards.title: guard for bounds
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Validate indices before subscripting.
Takeaway: Prevent out-of-bounds crashes.
Trap: `arr[i]` will crash if i is invalid.

cards.title: loop cost awareness
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Know what your loop does per iteration.
Takeaway: Keep work constant-time where possible.
Trap: Calling `sorted()` inside a loop is often catastrophic.

cards.title: avoid work in UI thread
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t do heavy loops on the main thread.
Takeaway: Use background tasks for big work.
Trap: UI freezes are perceived as app bugs.

cards.title: switch with associated values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `switch` to unwrap associated values.
Takeaway: Safe and clear.
Trap: Don’t use `.some`/`.none` patterns when `if let` is simpler.

cards.title: guard + multiple conditions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Guard can combine multiple checks.
Takeaway: `guard a, b, let x else { return }`.
Trap: Overlong guard lines hurt readability—split them.

cards.title: if #available
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `if #available(iOS 17, *) { ... }`.
Takeaway: Guard new APIs.
Trap: Forgetting availability checks can crash on older OS versions.

cards.title: #available in guard
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can use availability in guard.
Takeaway: Early-exit when API isn’t available.
Trap: Don’t overuse availability checks—centralize when possible.

cards.title: switch with availability
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer availability checks around new APIs.
Takeaway: Keep your code compatible.
Trap: Calling new API in a default branch still breaks older OS.

cards.title: looping with defer
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `defer` inside a loop runs each iteration when scope ends.
Takeaway: Useful for per-iteration cleanup.
Trap: Don’t accumulate defers in long scopes unintentionally.

cards.title: defer order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Multiple `defer` blocks run in reverse order.
Takeaway: Understand cleanup order.
Trap: Assuming FIFO leads to subtle bugs.

cards.title: guard for resources
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Acquire resource then `defer` release.
Takeaway: Safe cleanup even on early returns.
Trap: Don’t `return` before the resource is acquired.

cards.title: switch as validator
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use switch to validate input categories.
Takeaway: Clear rules in one place.
Trap: Don’t hide invalid values in default silently.

cards.title: loop with continue for validation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Validate early and `continue`.
Takeaway: Keeps main logic clean.
Trap: Be careful: `continue` skips the rest of the iteration.

cards.title: while vs for choice
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `for` for known ranges, `while` for unknown iterations.
Takeaway: Communicates intent.
Trap: Using `while` for simple counting loops hides structure.

cards.title: infinite loop guard
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Always ensure a loop changes something that affects its condition.
Takeaway: Prevent infinite loops.
Trap: Debugging an infinite loop on device is painful.

cards.title: switch + default logging
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If you must use default, consider logging.
Takeaway: Helps detect unexpected cases.
Trap: Don’t spam logs in production for normal flows.

cards.title: control flow readability
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer the simplest construct that reads clearly.
Takeaway: Maintenance beats cleverness.
Trap: Overusing pattern tricks confuses teammates.

cards.title: nested if flattening
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Replace nested ifs with guard/early returns.
Takeaway: Less indentation.
Trap: Don’t turn everything into guards—balance readability.

cards.title: compound conditions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Break complex conditions into named booleans.
Takeaway: `let isValid = ...`.
Trap: Mega-conditions are hard to test and debug.

cards.title: switch with multiple patterns
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A case can match multiple patterns: `case 1, 2, 3:`.
Takeaway: Cleaner than repeated code.
Trap: Don’t over-group unrelated values.

cards.title: looping over optionals
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `for x in optionalArray ?? []` to loop safely.
Takeaway: Avoid optional loops.
Trap: Make sure fallback `[]` matches intent (nil vs empty).

cards.title: guard let self in closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `[weak self]` + `guard let self else { return }`.
Takeaway: Avoid retain cycles.
Trap: Don’t use `unowned` unless lifetime is guaranteed.

cards.title: switch vs polymorphism
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If switch grows, consider polymorphism (protocols).
Takeaway: Move behavior into types.
Trap: Premature abstraction is also bad—switch is fine when small.

cards.title: return in closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `return` inside a closure returns from the closure, not the outer function.
Takeaway: Know your scopes.
Trap: In `forEach`, `return` does not break the loop.

cards.title: break out of forEach
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can’t break `forEach`.
Takeaway: Use `for-in` if you need early exit.
Trap: People assume `return` breaks—wrong.

cards.title: switch for parsing digits
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use switch cases for character categories.
Takeaway: Parsing becomes explicit.
Trap: Don’t forget `default` for unexpected chars.

cards.title: guard vs assert
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use guard for runtime user/data validation; assert for developer assumptions.
Takeaway: Different audiences.
Trap: Asserts may not run in release builds.

cards.title: assert basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `assert(condition)` checks in debug.
Takeaway: Catch programmer errors early.
Trap: Don’t rely on assert for production validation.

cards.title: precondition basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `precondition` can enforce conditions in release.
Takeaway: Use for truly required invariants.
Trap: It can crash users—use carefully.

cards.title: Control Flow — fatalError
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `fatalError()` stops execution immediately.
Takeaway: Use for impossible states.
Trap: If it’s possible in production, it will crash real users.

cards.title: control flow checklist
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Choose: `if` for few branches, `switch` for many cases, `guard` for required conditions.
Takeaway: Intent-driven code.
Trap: Mixing all three in one tiny function is overkill.

modules.title: 3. Functions & Closures
modules.moduleDescription: Functions, parameters/labels, return values, closures, capturing, @escaping, and common pitfalls.

cards.title: Why functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Functions package reusable behavior under a name.
Takeaway: Less duplication and easier testing.
Trap: Giant “doEverything()” functions become unmaintainable.

cards.title: Function signature
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A function’s signature includes name, parameter labels, and types.
Takeaway: Labels affect overload resolution.
Trap: Changing an external label is a breaking API change.

cards.title: Void return
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Functions with no meaningful return use `Void` (`()`).
Takeaway: You can omit `-> Void`.
Trap: `return` still works for early exit in Void functions.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — Parameter labels
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift uses external parameter labels by default.
Takeaway: Call sites read like sentences.
Trap: Poor labels make APIs painful to use.

cards.title: Omit labels with _
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `_` to omit an external label.
Takeaway: Great for math-like APIs.
Trap: Omitting labels can reduce readability in business code.

cards.title: Default parameters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Parameters can have default values.
Takeaway: Fewer overloads needed.
Trap: Defaults can create ambiguous calls when combined with overloads.

cards.title: Variadic parameters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `func sum(_ nums: Int...)` accepts many values.
Takeaway: Call with `sum(1,2,3)`.
Trap: To pass an array, use `sum(arr...)`, not `sum(arr)`.

cards.title: Inout basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `inout` lets a function mutate an argument.
Takeaway: Call with `&value`.
Trap: `inout` is copy-in/copy-out, not true reference passing.

cards.title: Inout restrictions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can’t pass temporary values as `inout`.
Takeaway: It must be a mutable variable.
Trap: `&obj.computedProp` doesn’t work—store in a var first.

cards.title: Overloads
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift can overload functions by parameter labels/types.
Takeaway: Use overloads to improve call-site clarity.
Trap: Too many overloads hurts discoverability.

cards.title: Return type overload trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Overloading by return type alone doesn’t work.
Takeaway: The compiler can’t pick a function from return type only.
Trap: You’ll get “ambiguous use” errors.

cards.title: Named return tuples
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Return multiple values with a named tuple.
Takeaway: `-> (min: Int, max: Int)` improves readability.
Trap: For complex data, prefer a struct.

cards.title: Functions as values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Functions are first-class values.
Takeaway: Store them in variables or pass as arguments.
Trap: Don’t call the function when you mean to pass it (`inc` vs `inc()`).

cards.title: Typealias for closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `typealias Handler = (Result<Data,Error>) -> Void`.
Takeaway: Cleaner signatures.
Trap: Don’t create typealiases for one-off trivial closures.

cards.title: Closures basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A closure is an unnamed function value.
Takeaway: Common for callbacks and transforms.
Trap: Closures can capture state and create memory cycles.

cards.title: Closure syntax
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `{ (x: Int) -> Int in x + 1 }`.
Takeaway: Parameters/return before `in`, body after.
Trap: Forgetting `in` when explicitly listing parameters is a compile error.

cards.title: Trailing closure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If the last argument is a closure, it can be trailing.
Takeaway: `arr.map { $0 * 2 }`.
Trap: With multiple closures, trailing syntax can get confusing.

cards.title: Shorthand args $0
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `$0`, `$1` for short closures.
Takeaway: Great for one-liners.
Trap: Long closures with $0 become unreadable—name parameters.

cards.title: Implicit return
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Single-expression closures can omit `return`.
Takeaway: `{ $0 + 1 }`.
Trap: Add a second statement and you must use `return` again.

cards.title: Escaping closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@escaping` means the closure can outlive the function call.
Takeaway: Typical for async APIs.
Trap: Escaping closures require explicit `self.` in classes.

cards.title: Non-escaping default
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Parameters are non-escaping by default.
Takeaway: Safer and often faster.
Trap: You can’t store a non-escaping closure for later use.

cards.title: Capture list
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use capture lists like `[weak self]`.
Takeaway: Prevent retain cycles.
Trap: `unowned` crashes if `self` is already deallocated.

cards.title: Weak self pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `[weak self] in guard let self else { return }`.
Takeaway: Safe UI callbacks.
Trap: Don’t silently ignore nil self if work must complete—design accordingly.

cards.title: Strong self inside closure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let self else { return }` makes `self` strong in the scope.
Takeaway: Prevents self disappearing mid-block.
Trap: It still avoids long-term cycles when captured weakly.

cards.title: Capture by value
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `[x] in` captures a snapshot of `x`.
Takeaway: Freezes a value for later.
Trap: If you wanted live updates, capturing by value is wrong.

cards.title: Retain cycle scenario
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If `self` stores a closure and the closure captures `self`, that’s a cycle.
Takeaway: Break it with `weak self` or redesign ownership.
Trap: Cycles leak memory without crashing immediately.

cards.title: Autoclosure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@autoclosure` wraps an expression into a closure.
Takeaway: Useful for `assert`-like APIs.
Trap: It can hide work—avoid in casual APIs.

cards.title: Throwing functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mark with `throws` and call with `try`.
Takeaway: Use for recoverable failures.
Trap: `try?` hides error details by turning them into nil.

cards.title: try? vs do/catch
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try?` returns an optional; `do/catch` keeps error info.
Takeaway: Use `do/catch` when you need the reason.
Trap: Swallowing errors makes debugging painful.

cards.title: rethrows
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `rethrows` throws only if the closure argument throws.
Takeaway: Useful for higher-order functions.
Trap: You can’t throw your own error from a `rethrows` function unless the closure throws.

cards.title: defer
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `defer` runs when leaving scope.
Takeaway: Great for cleanup.
Trap: Multiple defers run in reverse order (LIFO).

cards.title: Never vs Void
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Never` means “does not return” (e.g., `fatalError`).
Takeaway: Helps control-flow analysis.
Trap: Don’t confuse `Never` with `Void`—Void returns normally.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — Mutating methods
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Struct methods that change `self` must be `mutating`.
Takeaway: Makes value semantics explicit.
Trap: You can’t call a mutating method on a `let` struct instance.

cards.title: Nested functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can define functions inside functions.
Takeaway: Hide helpers locally.
Trap: Too much nesting hurts readability and debugging.

cards.title: Higher-order functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `map/filter/reduce` take closures.
Takeaway: Express transformations succinctly.
Trap: Don’t force functional style when a loop is clearer.

cards.title: map vs for
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `map` returns a new array; it’s not for side effects.
Takeaway: Use `for` for side effects.
Trap: `map { print($0) }` is a smell.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — filter
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `filter` keeps items where predicate is true.
Takeaway: Great for selection.
Trap: Filtering repeatedly on large arrays can be expensive.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — reduce
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `reduce` accumulates into one value.
Takeaway: Great for sums or building dictionaries.
Trap: The initial value matters—choose carefully.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — compactMap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `compactMap` transforms and drops nil results.
Takeaway: Perfect for parsing.
Trap: `map` would keep nils, producing `[T?]`.

cards.title: flatMap sequences
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `flatMap` flattens nested sequences.
Takeaway: `[[1,2],[3]] -> [1,2,3]`.
Trap: Don’t confuse with optional flatMap.

cards.title: Sorting with closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `sorted(by:)` takes a comparator closure.
Takeaway: Custom ordering is easy.
Trap: Comparator must be strict and consistent.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — sorted vs sort
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `sorted()` returns a new array; `sort()` mutates.
Takeaway: Choose based on need.
Trap: Calling `sorted()` and expecting the original to change.

cards.title: forEach trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `forEach` can’t `break` or `continue`.
Takeaway: Use `for-in` if you need control flow.
Trap: `return` in `forEach` returns from closure, not outer scope.

cards.title: Operator functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Operators like `+` can be passed as functions.
Takeaway: `nums.reduce(0, +)`.
Trap: Only do this when it improves readability.

cards.title: KeyPath in map
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can map using key paths: `users.map(\.name)`.
Takeaway: Concise property extraction.
Trap: Works only for direct property access.

cards.title: Escaping + self. rule
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In escaping closures, explicit `self.` is required in classes.
Takeaway: Forces you to notice captures.
Trap: Adding `self.` everywhere blindly defeats the point.

cards.title: Completion handler pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Common async API: `completion(Result<Success, Error>)`.
Takeaway: One channel for success/failure.
Trap: Don’t use `(data, error)` pairs—easy to misuse.

cards.title: Result type
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Result<Success, Failure: Error>` encodes outcome.
Takeaway: Clear success/failure.
Trap: Don’t wrap `Result` inside another optional unless necessary.

cards.title: Callback must be called
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Call completion on every path.
Takeaway: Avoid “hanging” UI.
Trap: Early return without calling completion is a classic bug.

cards.title: Main thread UI updates
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Update UIKit/SwiftUI state on the main actor.
Takeaway: Use `@MainActor` or `MainActor.run`.
Trap: Updating UI from background causes warnings/crashes.

cards.title: DispatchQueue vs async/await
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer async/await when possible, but know GCD.
Takeaway: Many APIs still use callbacks.
Trap: Mixing styles randomly makes code harder to follow.

cards.title: Closure capture of reference types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Closures capture references for classes.
Takeaway: Mutations inside are shared.
Trap: Assuming capture makes a copy of a class.

cards.title: Closure capture of value types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Value types are captured by value (copy-on-write may apply).
Takeaway: Often safe and predictable.
Trap: Capturing a struct that contains class references still shares those references.

cards.title: Lazy var closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `lazy var` often uses a closure to initialize.
Takeaway: Work happens on first access.
Trap: `lazy` is not thread-safe by default.

cards.title: Computed properties are functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Computed properties run code each access.
Takeaway: Keep them cheap.
Trap: Heavy computed properties inside UI rendering cause jank.

cards.title: Default argument evaluation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Default args are evaluated at call time.
Takeaway: They can use current values.
Trap: Don’t put expensive work in defaults.

cards.title: Overload with labels
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Labels can distinguish overloads.
Takeaway: `move(to:)` vs `move(by:)`.
Trap: Too many label variants confuse users.

cards.title: Variadic + array spread
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `...` to pass an array to variadic.
Takeaway: `sum(nums...)`.
Trap: `sum(nums)` passes the array as a single argument (doesn’t compile).

cards.title: Escaping closure stored property
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stored closure properties are effectively escaping.
Takeaway: Always think about captures.
Trap: Stored closures are a common source of retain cycles.

cards.title: Using self in struct closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In structs, capturing `self` is a value capture.
Takeaway: Usually safer.
Trap: If the struct contains reference members, you can still leak indirectly.

cards.title: @discardableResult
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `@discardableResult` to allow ignoring returns.
Takeaway: Helpful for builder-style APIs.
Trap: Don’t hide important results—warnings exist for a reason.

cards.title: Pure functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pure functions have no side effects.
Takeaway: Easier to test and reason about.
Trap: “Pure” is a design goal, not a hard rule everywhere.

cards.title: Side effects location
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep side effects at the edges (UI, IO).
Takeaway: Core logic stays testable.
Trap: Side effects buried in helpers create hidden coupling.

cards.title: Function naming
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use verb-based names: `load`, `save`, `calculate`.
Takeaway: Communicates intent.
Trap: Names like `doStuff()` are useless.

cards.title: API readability labels
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Labels like `to`, `from`, `with` improve call sites.
Takeaway: Calls read like English.
Trap: Redundant labels (`withValue value:`) add noise.

cards.title: Method vs function
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A method is a function on a type.
Takeaway: Instance vs static matters.
Trap: Mixing instance and static responsibilities leads to messy design.

cards.title: Static functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `static` belongs to the type, not instances.
Takeaway: Great for factories.
Trap: Don’t use static just to avoid passing dependencies.

cards.title: Passing initializers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Type.init` can be passed as a function.
Takeaway: `strings.compactMap(Int.init)`.
Trap: If init is failable/throwing, the function type changes.

cards.title: Escaping + async
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many callback APIs can be wrapped into async/await.
Takeaway: Cleaner, linear code.
Trap: Bridging must resume continuation exactly once.

cards.title: Continuations (concept)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Continuations bridge callbacks to async.
Takeaway: Use checked continuations for safety.
Trap: Resuming twice or never is a bug.

cards.title: Closure parameter naming
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Name closure parameters when logic isn’t trivial.
Takeaway: `map { user in user.name }`.
Trap: `$0` everywhere becomes unreadable.

cards.title: Multi-closure calls
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer explicit labels when a function takes multiple closures.
Takeaway: Improves clarity.
Trap: Trailing closure syntax can mislead with multiple closures.

cards.title: Escaping and lifetime
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Escaping closures may run after the caller is gone.
Takeaway: Design for cancellation/weak refs.
Trap: Updating UI after a screen dismisses is a common issue.

cards.title: Closures and memory
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Closures store captured values.
Takeaway: Capturing large objects increases memory.
Trap: Capturing `self` just to access one value—pass the value instead.

cards.title: Generic functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Generics allow one function to work with many types.
Takeaway: `func swapTwo<T>(_ a: inout T, _ b: inout T)`.
Trap: Generics preserve type safety—unlike `Any`.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — Generic constraints
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Add constraints with `where` or `T: Protocol`.
Takeaway: Enables operations like `<` for Comparable.
Trap: Over-constraining reduces reuse.

cards.title: Functions & Closures — Same-type constraints
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `where T.Element == Int` pins a type.
Takeaway: Useful for specialized utilities.
Trap: Can unintentionally exclude valid types.

cards.title: Currying concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A function can return another function.
Takeaway: Useful for configuration.
Trap: Overuse makes code hard for teams.

cards.title: Returning closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Factories can return closures.
Takeaway: Configurable behaviors.
Trap: Returned closures can capture state and keep objects alive.

cards.title: Capturing self in returned closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If you return a closure that captures `self`, you extend its lifetime.
Takeaway: Be intentional about ownership.
Trap: Hidden memory leaks in “factory” helpers.

cards.title: Defer in closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `defer` inside a closure runs when the closure returns.
Takeaway: Cleanup still works.
Trap: It does not wait for the outer function.

cards.title: Testing closures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Test logic by injecting closures.
Takeaway: Dependency injection becomes easy.
Trap: Over-injecting closures can make APIs awkward.

cards.title: Higher-order API design
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep closure APIs small and well-named.
Takeaway: Users should understand what the closure does.
Trap: “callback soup” with unclear semantics.

modules.title: 4. Collections
modules.moduleDescription: Array/Dictionary/Set, iteration, transformation (map/filter/reduce), performance and safety traps.

cards.title: Array basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Arrays store ordered elements of one type.
Takeaway: Use `[T]` and keep a stable order.
Trap: Index out of range crashes.

cards.title: Create arrays
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Create with literals: `let a = [1,2,3]`.
Takeaway: Type inferred from elements.
Trap: Empty literal `[]` needs a type context.

cards.title: Empty array typed
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `var a: [Int] = []` creates an empty typed array.
Takeaway: Now you can append.
Trap: `let a = []` won’t compile (unknown element type).

cards.title: append
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `append(_:)` adds to the end.
Takeaway: Amortized O(1).
Trap: Requires `var` array, not `let`.

cards.title: append(contentsOf:)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `append(contentsOf:)` adds many elements.
Takeaway: Better than `a = a + b` for large arrays.
Trap: Don’t forget it mutates, so `a` must be `var`.

cards.title: insert(at:)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `insert(_:at:)` inserts at an index.
Takeaway: Useful for UI lists.
Trap: It’s O(n); heavy use is slow on large arrays.

cards.title: remove(at:)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `remove(at:)` removes and returns the element.
Takeaway: Great when you need the removed item.
Trap: Invalid index crashes.

cards.title: removeLast
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `removeLast()` removes last element.
Takeaway: Fast.
Trap: Crashes if the array is empty—check `isEmpty`.

cards.title: first/last are optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `first` and `last` return optionals.
Takeaway: Arrays can be empty.
Trap: Force-unwrapping is a common crash.

cards.title: count vs isEmpty
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `isEmpty` over `count == 0`.
Takeaway: More expressive.
Trap: Some collections compute count more expensively.

cards.title: contains
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `contains(_:)` checks membership.
Takeaway: For arrays it’s O(n).
Trap: If you need fast membership, use a Set.

cards.title: safe indexing idea
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Standard subscripting `a[i]` is unsafe.
Takeaway: Consider a `safe` subscript that returns optional.
Trap: Silently returning nil can hide logic errors—log/test.

cards.title: Iteration for-in
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `for x in a { ... }` iterates elements.
Takeaway: Safe and simple.
Trap: Mutating array structure while iterating leads to bugs.

cards.title: Collections — enumerated()
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `for (i,x) in a.enumerated()`.
Takeaway: Index + element.
Trap: `i` is an offset, not always the true index type for all collections.

cards.title: indices
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `a.indices` for safe index iteration.
Takeaway: Works with slices.
Trap: Hardcoding `0..<count` breaks for some collections/slices.

cards.title: map
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `map` transforms each element and returns a new array.
Takeaway: Pure transform.
Trap: Don’t use `map` for side effects.

cards.title: Collections — compactMap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `compactMap` transforms and drops nils.
Takeaway: Great for parsing.
Trap: Don’t confuse with `filter` (different intent).

cards.title: Collections — filter
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `filter` keeps elements where predicate is true.
Takeaway: Clear selection.
Trap: Re-filtering big arrays often can be expensive.

cards.title: Collections — reduce
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `reduce` folds into one value.
Takeaway: Sums, concatenation, building dictionaries.
Trap: Wrong initial accumulator gives wrong results.

cards.title: Collections — sorted vs sort
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `sorted()` returns new array; `sort()` mutates.
Takeaway: Choose based on need.
Trap: Expecting `sorted()` to change original array.

cards.title: reversed()
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `reversed()` returns a reversed view/collection.
Takeaway: Convert to Array if you need one: `Array(a.reversed())`.
Trap: Assuming it’s always an Array.

cards.title: slices are ArraySlice
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `a[0..<3]` returns `ArraySlice`.
Takeaway: Convert to Array when needed.
Trap: Slices can retain the original buffer (memory).

cards.title: ArraySlice memory trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Small slices may keep a large array alive.
Takeaway: Use `Array(slice)` to copy just what you need.
Trap: Unexpected memory growth.

cards.title: reserveCapacity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `reserveCapacity` reduces reallocations for many appends.
Takeaway: Useful when size is known.
Trap: Premature optimization—profile first.

cards.title: Collections — Value semantics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Array is a value type (copy-on-write).
Takeaway: Copies are cheap until mutation.
Trap: Mutating one copy can trigger a full buffer copy.

cards.title: Dictionary basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dictionaries map keys to values.
Takeaway: Type is `[Key: Value]`.
Trap: Keys must be Hashable.

cards.title: Collections — Dictionary lookup optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key]` returns an optional.
Takeaway: Key may be missing.
Trap: Force unwrap causes crashes.

cards.title: Insert/update dict
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key] = value` inserts or updates.
Takeaway: Simple API.
Trap: Overwriting existing values may lose data—be intentional.

cards.title: updateValue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `updateValue(_:forKey:)` returns the old value.
Takeaway: Lets you detect replacement.
Trap: Returned value is optional—handle it.

cards.title: removeValue
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `removeValue(forKey:)` removes and returns old value.
Takeaway: Great for caches.
Trap: Returns nil if key didn’t exist.

cards.title: Dictionary keys/values views
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict.keys` and `dict.values` are views.
Takeaway: They’re not arrays by default.
Trap: Convert if you need sorting: `Array(dict.keys).sorted()`.

cards.title: Dictionary iteration order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t rely on dictionary iteration order.
Takeaway: Sort keys for deterministic UI.
Trap: It may look stable on your machine, but don’t depend on it.

cards.title: Dictionary default
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `dict[key, default: 0] += 1`.
Takeaway: Perfect for counters.
Trap: This mutates the dictionary; it must be `var`.

cards.title: mapValues
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `mapValues` transforms values, keeps keys.
Takeaway: Useful for derived dictionaries.
Trap: It doesn’t change key type.

cards.title: merging
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `merging`/`merge` to combine dictionaries.
Takeaway: Provide conflict resolution.
Trap: Silent overwrites without a resolution closure.

cards.title: Dictionary(grouping:by:)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Group items by a key into `[Key: [Element]]`.
Takeaway: Great for sections.
Trap: Group key must be Hashable.

cards.title: Set basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set stores unique elements.
Takeaway: Fast membership checks.
Trap: No stable order.

cards.title: Create Set
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `let s: Set<Int> = [1,2,3]`.
Takeaway: Needs type context to distinguish from Array.
Trap: `let s = [1,2,3]` is an Array.

cards.title: Set insert
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `insert` adds an element.
Takeaway: Returns (inserted, memberAfterInsert).
Trap: Ignoring the return can hide duplicate logic errors.

cards.title: Set operations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `union`, `intersection`, `subtracting`.
Takeaway: Powerful set math.
Trap: Confusing `subtracting` with symmetric difference.

cards.title: Hashable requirement
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set elements and dict keys must be Hashable.
Takeaway: Make your models Hashable carefully.
Trap: If hash/== disagree, Sets/Dictionaries break.

cards.title: Collections — Custom Hashable trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t include mutable fields in hash.
Takeaway: Stable identity fields only.
Trap: Mutating a hashed field after insertion breaks lookups.

cards.title: Equatable vs Hashable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Hashable implies Equatable.
Takeaway: Equality must match hash semantics.
Trap: Implementing one without the other correctly causes bugs.

cards.title: Optionals in dictionaries
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key]` is optional even if Value isn’t.
Takeaway: Missing key is the reason.
Trap: If Value itself is optional, you can get `T??`.

cards.title: Collections — Double optional trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If Value is `T?`, lookup returns `T??`.
Takeaway: Distinguish “missing key” vs “stored nil”.
Trap: Prefer avoiding optional values in dictionaries unless necessary.

cards.title: Stable ordering for UI
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For UI, convert keys to array and sort.
Takeaway: Deterministic lists.
Trap: Sorting every render is expensive—cache if needed.

cards.title: zip
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `zip(a,b)` pairs elements until the shorter ends.
Takeaway: Great for parallel iteration.
Trap: Extra elements in the longer sequence are dropped.

cards.title: stride
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `stride(from:to:by:)` is great for stepping.
Takeaway: Avoid manual index math.
Trap: `to` excludes the end; `through` includes it.

cards.title: lazy sequences
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.lazy` defers work in chains.
Takeaway: Helpful for large pipelines.
Trap: Converting to Array forces evaluation immediately.

cards.title: Big-O awareness
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Choose collection types based on operation costs.
Takeaway: Array for order, Set for membership, Dictionary for key lookup.
Trap: Using Array for frequent contains is slow.

cards.title: Remove duplicates fast
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Array(Set(array))` removes duplicates quickly.
Takeaway: Simple approach.
Trap: Order is lost—use stable dedupe if order matters.

cards.title: Stable dedupe
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep a Set of seen IDs and filter once.
Takeaway: Preserves first-seen order.
Trap: Don’t use indices as IDs; use stable identifiers.

cards.title: randomElement
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `randomElement()` returns optional.
Takeaway: Collection might be empty.
Trap: Force unwrap can crash.

cards.title: shuffle vs shuffled
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `shuffle()` mutates; `shuffled()` returns new.
Takeaway: Same pattern as sort/sorted.
Trap: Calling `shuffled()` and expecting original to change.

cards.title: prefix/suffix
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `prefix(n)`/`suffix(n)` return slices.
Takeaway: Convert to Array if needed.
Trap: Slice keeps the original buffer alive.

cards.title: dropFirst/dropLast
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dropFirst()`/`dropLast()` return subsequences.
Takeaway: Non-mutating views.
Trap: They don’t change the original collection.

cards.title: Collection vs Sequence
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sequence is one-pass, Collection is multi-pass with indices.
Takeaway: Prefer Collection when you need count/indexing.
Trap: Assuming all sequences have O(1) count.

cards.title: Array + operator
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `a + b` creates a new array.
Takeaway: Convenient for small arrays.
Trap: For big arrays, prefer `append(contentsOf:)` to avoid copies.

cards.title: Contains where
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `contains(where:)` searches by predicate.
Takeaway: Useful for custom membership.
Trap: Still O(n) for arrays—don’t overuse in hot paths.

cards.title: first(where:)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `first(where:)` finds first match.
Takeaway: Clear intent.
Trap: Returns optional; handle nil.

cards.title: allSatisfy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `allSatisfy` checks if all items match.
Takeaway: Cleaner than a manual loop.
Trap: Empty collections return true (vacuous truth).

cards.title: anySatisfy via contains
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `contains(where:)` is “any satisfy”.
Takeaway: Easy readability.
Trap: Don’t confuse with `allSatisfy`.

cards.title: Dictionary as cache
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dictionary is a great in-memory cache.
Takeaway: Fast lookup.
Trap: Unbounded caches grow memory—use limits/eviction.

cards.title: Set for visited
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use Set for visited IDs in graph-like logic.
Takeaway: Prevent duplicates.
Trap: IDs must be stable and Hashable.

cards.title: Nested collections
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nested collections are normal (e.g., `[Section: [Row]]`).
Takeaway: Model data for the UI.
Trap: Deep nesting makes code hard—use models.

cards.title: JSON key constraints
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: JSON object keys are strings.
Takeaway: `[Int: X]` doesn’t map directly to JSON keys.
Trap: You may need to convert keys to String.

cards.title: Set Codable note
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sets encode like arrays.
Takeaway: Fine for storage.
Trap: Order can change after decoding.

cards.title: Performance trap: insert at front
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inserting/removing at the front of an Array is O(n).
Takeaway: Prefer different data structures or algorithms.
Trap: It “works” in tests but slows down in production.

cards.title: Mutating while iterating
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t change collection structure while iterating.
Takeaway: Collect changes then apply.
Trap: Indexes shift and cause subtle bugs.

cards.title: views are not copies
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `keys`, `values`, slices are views.
Takeaway: Cheap to create.
Trap: They can retain underlying storage.

cards.title: Prefer empty over optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer empty collections over optional collections.
Takeaway: Fewer unwraps.
Trap: Use optional only when “no value” differs from “empty”.

modules.title: 5. Optionals & Safety
modules.moduleDescription: Optionals, safe unwrapping patterns, avoiding crashes, and defensive Swift habits.

cards.title: Optionals meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `T?` means “a T value or nil”.
Takeaway: Use optionals to represent absence safely.
Trap: `nil` is not the same as `0` or an empty string.

cards.title: Optional vs non-optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `String` is always a string; `String?` may be nil.
Takeaway: Avoid making everything optional.
Trap: Optional-by-default creates unwrap-heavy code.

cards.title: nil needs a type
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `nil` needs a type context.
Takeaway: `var x: Int? = nil` is valid.
Trap: `let x = nil` won’t compile (unknown type).

cards.title: Optionals & Safety — if let unwrap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if let v = opt { ... }` unwraps safely.
Takeaway: Inside, `v` is non-optional.
Trap: `v` exists only in the if scope.

cards.title: if let shorthand
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift supports `if let opt { ... }` when names match.
Takeaway: Cleaner unwrapping.
Trap: Works only when the variable name stays the same.

cards.title: Optionals & Safety — guard let unwrap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let v = opt else { return }`.
Takeaway: Keeps code flat.
Trap: `guard` must exit the current scope.

cards.title: guard let shorthand
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let opt else { return }` is allowed in newer Swift.
Takeaway: Less repetition.
Trap: Requires modern Swift toolchains.

cards.title: Optionals & Safety — Force unwrap !
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid `opt!` unless you’re 100% sure it’s not nil.
Takeaway: Prefer safe unwrapping.
Trap: `!` crashes at runtime when nil appears.

cards.title: Implicitly unwrapped T!
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `T!` is used for values set later (often IBOutlets).
Takeaway: Treat it as optional that can crash.
Trap: Accessing before it’s set is a crash.

cards.title: Optionals & Safety — Nil-coalescing ??
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `opt ?? fallback` provides a default.
Takeaway: Simple safe fallback.
Trap: Use parentheses when mixing with other operators.

cards.title: Optional chaining
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `a?.b?.c` returns nil if any link is nil.
Takeaway: Safe deep access.
Trap: The result is still optional even if the property isn’t.

cards.title: Chaining method calls
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `obj?.doWork()` may not run if obj is nil.
Takeaway: Side effects might not happen.
Trap: Don’t rely on optional chaining for critical operations.

cards.title: Multiple bindings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if let a = aOpt, let b = bOpt {}` unwraps both.
Takeaway: Unwrap related values together.
Trap: Too many bindings in one line hurts readability.

cards.title: Guard multiple
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let a = aOpt, let b = bOpt else { return }`.
Takeaway: Validates inputs early.
Trap: Split long guards into smaller checks.

cards.title: switch on optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `switch opt { case .some(let v): ... case .none: ... }`.
Takeaway: Explicit optional handling.
Trap: Overkill when `if let` is simpler.

cards.title: map on optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `opt.map(f)` applies f if opt isn’t nil.
Takeaway: Functional unwrapping.
Trap: Result remains optional.

cards.title: flatMap on optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `opt.flatMap(f)` avoids nested optionals.
Takeaway: Use when f returns an optional.
Trap: Don’t confuse with sequence flatMap.

cards.title: try? returns optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try?` turns `throws` into an optional.
Takeaway: Error becomes nil.
Trap: You lose the error reason.

cards.title: try! is risky
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try!` crashes if an error is thrown.
Takeaway: Use only when failure is impossible.
Trap: “Impossible” often becomes possible in production.

cards.title: as? vs as!
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `as?` over `as!`.
Takeaway: Safe casting avoids crashes.
Trap: `as!` is a crash waiting to happen.

cards.title: URL(string:) optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `URL(string:)` returns `URL?`.
Takeaway: Validate URLs.
Trap: Force unwrapping bad URLs crashes.

cards.title: Int(str) optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Int("123")` returns `Int?`.
Takeaway: Parse safely.
Trap: User input often includes spaces—trim first.

cards.title: Distinguish nil vs empty
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `nil` means missing; empty collection means present but empty.
Takeaway: Prefer empty collections for API design.
Trap: Returning nil instead of `[]` adds unwrap burden.

cards.title: Avoid optional collections
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `[]` over `[T]?` when possible.
Takeaway: Simplifies callers.
Trap: Use optional only when absence is semantically different.

cards.title: Dictionary lookup is optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key]` is optional even if `Value` isn’t.
Takeaway: Missing key is normal.
Trap: Force unwrapping dict lookups is a common crash.

cards.title: Setting dict value to nil
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `dict[key] = nil` removes the key.
Takeaway: Not the same as storing nil.
Trap: If you need to store nil, the Value type must be optional.

cards.title: Optionals & Safety — Double optional trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: With `Value = T?`, lookup returns `T??`.
Takeaway: Differentiate missing key vs stored nil.
Trap: Avoid optional values in dict unless necessary.

cards.title: Safe array access
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Validate indices before subscripting.
Takeaway: Prevent out-of-range crashes.
Trap: `arr[i]` will crash on invalid i.

cards.title: isEmpty before removeLast
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check `isEmpty` before removing.
Takeaway: Avoid crashes.
Trap: `removeLast()` on empty array crashes.

cards.title: RandomElement optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `randomElement()` returns optional.
Takeaway: Empty collections exist.
Trap: Don’t force unwrap randomElement.

cards.title: UIImage(named:) optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `UIImage(named:)` returns optional.
Takeaway: Asset might be missing.
Trap: `!` crashes when asset name is wrong.

cards.title: Date parsing optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `DateFormatter.date(from:)` returns optional.
Takeaway: Input may not match format.
Trap: Don’t force unwrap user/server dates.

cards.title: Data to String optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `String(data:encoding:)` returns optional.
Takeaway: Encoding can fail.
Trap: Wrong encoding produces nil.

cards.title: Optional UI text
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide UI fallbacks: `label.text = name ?? "—"`.
Takeaway: Better UX.
Trap: Don’t show `Optional(...)` to users.

cards.title: print optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Printing optionals shows `Optional(x)`.
Takeaway: Fine for debug.
Trap: Don’t use debug output as user-facing text.

cards.title: weak self pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `[weak self]` in escaping closures.
Takeaway: Avoid retain cycles.
Trap: `unowned` can crash if self deallocates.

cards.title: guard self in closure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let self else { return }` after weak capture.
Takeaway: Safe use of self.
Trap: If self can be nil, decide whether work should be canceled.

cards.title: Unowned risks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `unowned` only when lifetime is guaranteed.
Takeaway: No optional unwrapping.
Trap: Wrong assumption = crash.

cards.title: Optionals and state modeling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t use optionals to represent complex state.
Takeaway: Prefer an enum state machine.
Trap: Multiple optionals create ambiguous states.

cards.title: Result vs Optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Optional gives no reason; `Result` does.
Takeaway: Use Result/throws for error detail.
Trap: Returning nil hides the failure cause.

cards.title: throws vs optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `throws` when failure reasons matter.
Takeaway: More debuggable APIs.
Trap: Overusing throws for normal control flow is noisy.

cards.title: assert vs guard
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `assert` for developer mistakes; `guard` for runtime validation.
Takeaway: Different audiences.
Trap: Asserts may not run in release builds.

cards.title: precondition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `precondition` can crash in release.
Takeaway: Use only for required invariants.
Trap: Don’t punish users for recoverable issues.

cards.title: Optionals & Safety — fatalError
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `fatalError()` stops execution.
Takeaway: Use for truly impossible states.
Trap: If it can happen, it will crash real users.

cards.title: Never type
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Never` indicates a function does not return.
Takeaway: Helps control flow.
Trap: Don’t confuse Never with Void.

cards.title: Guard + throw
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard condition else { throw Error }` validates cleanly.
Takeaway: Early-exit error paths.
Trap: Don’t throw for expected “no result” scenarios.

cards.title: Safe casting in switch
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `switch value { case let x as Int: ... }`.
Takeaway: Useful for debugging Any.
Trap: Heavy `Any` usage is an architecture smell.

cards.title: Optional binding shadowing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if let value = value` creates a new variable.
Takeaway: Inside, it’s non-optional.
Trap: Shadowing can confuse which variable you’re using.

cards.title: Shorthand binding (Swift 5.7+)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if let value { ... }` reduces repetition.
Takeaway: Cleaner code.
Trap: Requires modern toolchains.

cards.title: Nil as default argument
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `func f(x: Int? = nil)` can be convenient.
Takeaway: Optional parameters are sometimes fine.
Trap: Too many optional params makes APIs unclear.

cards.title: Prefer non-optional storage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Unwrap once, then store as non-optional.
Takeaway: Less `?` noise.
Trap: Carrying optionals everywhere increases bug surface.

cards.title: Safe URLComponents
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Build URLs with URLComponents.
Takeaway: Avoid invalid URLs.
Trap: `components.url` can still be nil—handle it.

cards.title: JSON decode errors
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Catch decoding errors and log payloads in debug.
Takeaway: Fast debugging.
Trap: Don’t log sensitive data in production.

cards.title: try? hides decoding reason
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try? decode` hides the exact DecodingError.
Takeaway: Use `do/catch` when debugging.
Trap: “It’s nil” gives no clue why.

cards.title: Nil vs 0
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: nil means unknown/absent; 0 is a real value.
Takeaway: Don’t use 0 as a sentinel.
Trap: Sentinel values cause edge-case bugs.

cards.title: Safe math domain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Validate inputs (divide by zero, sqrt of negative).
Takeaway: Prevent NaN/inf surprises.
Trap: Floating-point may not crash but still produces invalid results.

cards.title: Optional chaining return types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Optional chaining can produce `Void?` on method calls.
Takeaway: The call may not happen.
Trap: Don’t ignore that the method might be skipped.

cards.title: Optional bool trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Bool?` is three states, not two.
Takeaway: Use only if you need “unknown”.
Trap: Treating nil as false can be incorrect.

cards.title: Optional + equality
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Optionals compare when wrapped type is Equatable.
Takeaway: `nil == nil` is true.
Trap: Don’t use clever optional comparisons in business logic.

cards.title: Safe parsing pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let n = Int(str) else { ... }`.
Takeaway: Single entry point for validation.
Trap: Don’t forget trimming/locale details.

cards.title: Failable init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `init?` returns nil if creation fails.
Takeaway: Valid objects only.
Trap: It hides failure reasons—throws init can be better.

cards.title: Throws init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `init(...) throws` preserves error detail.
Takeaway: Better for debugging.
Trap: More call-site ceremony (try/catch).

cards.title: Optional images in UI
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Always handle missing images gracefully.
Takeaway: Provide placeholders.
Trap: Missing assets are common in early development.

cards.title: Thread-safety of optionals
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t mutate shared state from multiple tasks without protection.
Takeaway: Use actors/locks.
Trap: Data races create “random” bugs.

cards.title: Race conditions on state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Read+write sequences aren’t atomic.
Takeaway: Isolate state changes.
Trap: Two tasks can overwrite each other.

cards.title: State enums
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `enum LoadState { idle, loading, loaded, failed }`.
Takeaway: Fewer invalid combinations.
Trap: Multiple booleans/options create inconsistent states.

cards.title: Avoid silent failures
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If you drop a nil, make it intentional.
Takeaway: Log in debug or track metrics.
Trap: Silent nils can hide real production issues.

modules.title: 6. Structs & Enums
modules.moduleDescription: Value types, structs/enums, associated values, raw values, and modeling state safely.

cards.title: Struct vs class
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `struct` is a value type; `class` is a reference type.
Takeaway: Default to structs for models.
Trap: Expecting shared mutation with structs—copies are independent.

cards.title: Structs & Enums — Value semantics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Copying a struct copies its value.
Takeaway: Mutating one copy doesn’t change the other.
Trap: If a struct contains class references, those references are still shared.

cards.title: Structs & Enums — Mutating methods
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Struct methods that change `self` must be `mutating`.
Takeaway: Makes intent explicit.
Trap: You can’t call a mutating method on a `let` instance.

cards.title: Memberwise initializer
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Structs get a memberwise init automatically.
Takeaway: `User(name:age:)` for free.
Trap: Adding a custom init can remove the synthesized memberwise init.

cards.title: Custom init validation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Validate invariants inside `init`.
Takeaway: Types stay valid by construction.
Trap: Don’t leave partially valid objects around.

cards.title: Failable init?
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `init?` when creation can fail without an error reason.
Takeaway: Returns nil on failure.
Trap: Nil hides why it failed—sometimes `throws` is better.

cards.title: Throwing init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `init(...) throws` when you need failure reasons.
Takeaway: Better debuggability.
Trap: More ceremony at call sites (`try`).

cards.title: Stored vs computed
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stored properties hold data; computed properties compute it.
Takeaway: Use computed for derived values.
Trap: Heavy computed properties can cause performance issues.

cards.title: Property observers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `willSet`/`didSet` run on changes.
Takeaway: Great for syncing.
Trap: Observers don’t run for initial assignments during init.

cards.title: Static members
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `static` belongs to the type.
Takeaway: Constants and factories.
Trap: Don’t use static to hide global state.

cards.title: Enum basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Enums model a finite set of states.
Takeaway: Safer than strings/ints.
Trap: Don’t use an enum for open-ended values.

cards.title: Raw values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Enums can have raw values (`String`, `Int`).
Takeaway: Easy Codable for simple enums.
Trap: `Enum(rawValue:)` returns an optional.

cards.title: Associated values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Enum cases can carry data.
Takeaway: Great for state machines.
Trap: Different cases can store different types—switch carefully.

cards.title: Switch on enum
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `switch` to handle enum cases.
Takeaway: Exhaustiveness prevents missed states.
Trap: Adding `default` can hide missing cases.

cards.title: if case
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `if case .loaded(let x) = state {}` matches one case.
Takeaway: Short and focused.
Trap: Use `switch` when there are multiple meaningful cases.

cards.title: Structs & Enums — guard case
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard case .loaded(let x) = state else { return }`.
Takeaway: Flat happy path.
Trap: Don’t cram complex matching into one guard.

cards.title: CaseIterable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `CaseIterable` provides `allCases`.
Takeaway: Great for pickers and lists.
Trap: Doesn’t auto-work for enums with associated values.

cards.title: Equatable synthesis
