cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Struct/enum can auto-synthesize `Equatable`.
Takeaway: Great for tests and diffing.
Trap: All stored properties must be Equatable.

cards.title: Hashable synthesis
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Types can auto-synthesize `Hashable`.
Takeaway: Works for Set/Dictionary keys.
Trap: Hash must align with equality semantics.

cards.title: Custom Equatable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Implement custom `==` only when needed.
Takeaway: You can compare a subset of fields.
Trap: Surprising equality breaks assumptions and caching.

cards.title: Structs & Enums — Custom Hashable trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t include mutable fields in hash.
Takeaway: Use stable identity fields.
Trap: Mutating a hashed field after insertion breaks lookups.

cards.title: Codable struct
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Codable` structs are ideal for JSON models.
Takeaway: Simple decoding/encoding.
Trap: Key mismatches cause decoding errors.

cards.title: Structs & Enums — CodingKeys
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `CodingKeys` to map JSON keys.
Takeaway: snake_case to camelCase.
Trap: Forgetting a key can break decoding if property isn’t optional.

cards.title: keyDecodingStrategy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.convertFromSnakeCase` reduces boilerplate.
Takeaway: Fewer CodingKeys.
Trap: It’s not perfect for all acronyms and weird server keys.

cards.title: dateDecodingStrategy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Choose a date decoding strategy.
Takeaway: `.iso8601` is common.
Trap: Server date formats often differ—test against real payloads.

cards.title: Enum Codable raw
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Raw-value enums can conform to Codable easily.
Takeaway: Clean wire format.
Trap: Unknown raw values will fail decoding unless handled.

cards.title: Structs & Enums — Unknown enum case
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Add a fallback case (custom decode) for unknown values.
Takeaway: Forward compatibility.
Trap: Silently mapping unknowns can hide server changes.

cards.title: Indirect enums
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `indirect` enables recursive enums.
Takeaway: Trees and expressions.
Trap: Use only when you need recursion.

cards.title: OptionSet vs enum
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `OptionSet` for combinable flags.
Takeaway: Multiple options at once.
Trap: An enum represents exactly one case, not a set of flags.

cards.title: Struct immutability
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `let` makes the whole struct immutable.
Takeaway: Safer defaults.
Trap: Even `var` properties can’t change on a `let` instance.

cards.title: Value builder methods
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Returning modified copies enables immutable “builder” style.
Takeaway: `withName(_:) -> Self`.
Trap: Too many copies can be expensive—measure when large.

cards.title: Copy-on-write reminder
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Standard collections use copy-on-write.
Takeaway: Copies are cheap until mutation.
Trap: Large mutations can trigger big copies.

cards.title: Identity vs equality
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Classes have identity (`===`), value types don’t.
Takeaway: Use `==` for value equality.
Trap: Trying to use `===` on structs won’t compile.

cards.title: Enum as screen state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use enums to model UI state.
Takeaway: Fewer invalid combinations.
Trap: Multiple booleans create impossible states.

cards.title: State machine transitions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep transitions explicit (switch on state).
Takeaway: Easier debugging.
Trap: Hidden transitions via scattered flags cause bugs.

cards.title: Nested types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Nest enums/structs for namespacing.
Takeaway: Keeps related types together.
Trap: Over-nesting makes code hard to navigate.

cards.title: Extensions for organization
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use extensions to group functionality.
Takeaway: Better file structure.
Trap: Extensions can’t add stored properties.

cards.title: Lazy in structs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `lazy var` works in structs.
Takeaway: Delayed initialization.
Trap: Requires a mutable instance (`var`) because lazy mutates on first access.

cards.title: Computed cost
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Computed properties run each access.
Takeaway: Keep them cheap.
Trap: Heavy computed props inside UI rendering cause jank.

cards.title: Observer recursion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Changing a property inside `didSet` can cause recursion.
Takeaway: Guard against loops.
Trap: Infinite loops can freeze the app.

cards.title: Enum methods
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Enums can have methods and computed properties.
Takeaway: Encapsulate behavior with state.
Trap: Don’t turn enums into giant god-types.

cards.title: Struct as config
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Configs are great as structs.
Takeaway: Predictable copying.
Trap: If config contains reference types, mutation can still leak through.

cards.title: Hashable for IDs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use stable IDs for Identifiable/Hashable.
Takeaway: Better diffing.
Trap: Generating new UUIDs every render breaks identity.

cards.title: Identifiable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Adopt `Identifiable` for SwiftUI lists.
Takeaway: Stable list diffs.
Trap: Using array indices as IDs breaks on insert/delete.

cards.title: Enum rawValue versioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t change raw values without migration.
Takeaway: Keep wire/storage compatibility.
Trap: Reordering cases can silently change auto-assigned raw values.

cards.title: Failable init vs validation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer throwing validation when you need reasons.
Takeaway: Better error handling.
Trap: Returning nil hides debugging info.

cards.title: Modeling errors
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Define `enum MyError: Error`.
Takeaway: Meaningful error cases.
Trap: A single `unknown` case is often too vague.

cards.title: Pattern matching with where
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `where` in switch cases for refinement.
Takeaway: Expressive logic.
Trap: Too clever patterns reduce readability.

cards.title: Enum + associated + Equatable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Associated-value enums can be Equatable if values are.
Takeaway: Great for state comparisons.
Trap: Large associated values make equality checks expensive.

cards.title: Decoding nested models
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compose Codable structs for nested JSON.
Takeaway: Clean mapping.
Trap: Deep nesting without models becomes brittle.

cards.title: Prefer explicit defaults
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide sensible defaults instead of making everything optional.
Takeaway: Simpler call sites.
Trap: Wrong defaults can hide invalid data.

cards.title: Struct thread-safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Value types are easier to share safely.
Takeaway: Less shared mutable state.
Trap: They can still contain reference types—watch inside.

cards.title: Enum for routing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use enums for navigation routes.
Takeaway: Type-safe routing.
Trap: Huge route enums can become unmanageable—modularize.

cards.title: Mirror is for debug
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Reflection (`Mirror`) is for debugging.
Takeaway: Don’t use it in core logic.
Trap: Reflection is slow and fragile.

cards.title: CustomStringConvertible
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Implement `description` for better logs.
Takeaway: Cleaner debug output.
Trap: Don’t do heavy work inside `description`.

cards.title: Comparable for sorting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Implement Comparable when a total order makes sense.
Takeaway: Enables `sorted()`.
Trap: Bad ordering breaks assumptions and UI sort results.

cards.title: Stable sorting semantics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Sorting should be consistent and transitive.
Takeaway: Predictable ordering.
Trap: Inconsistent comparator leads to undefined results.

cards.title: Enum in switch without default
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Avoid default when switching on enums.
Takeaway: Compiler forces updates on new cases.
Trap: Default hides missing cases.

cards.title: Two-phase init concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Initialize all stored properties before using self.
Takeaway: Swift enforces safety.
Trap: Accessing self too early is a compile error.

cards.title: Struct builder performance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Builder chains create copies.
Takeaway: Fine for small structs.
Trap: Large structs in tight loops can be slow.

cards.title: Case paths vs booleans
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer one enum over many flags.
Takeaway: Reduced state explosion.
Trap: Flags drift out of sync.

cards.title: Optional in models
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Make a property optional only if it can truly be missing.
Takeaway: Stronger invariants.
Trap: Optional everywhere means “I don’t know the contract”.

cards.title: Collection of enums
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Arrays of enums are great for heterogeneous UI rows.
Takeaway: Each case represents a row type.
Trap: Don’t put view logic inside the enum; keep it data-focused.

cards.title: Enum payload size
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep associated values reasonably small.
Takeaway: Better performance.
Trap: Huge payloads complicate equality and copying.

modules.title: 7. Classes & ARC
modules.moduleDescription: Reference types, ARC, retain cycles, weak/unowned, and leak prevention.

cards.title: Classes are reference types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `class` instances are shared by reference.
Takeaway: Assigning copies the reference, not the object.
Trap: Unexpected shared mutation is a common bug.

cards.title: Identity operator ===
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `===` checks if two references point to the same object.
Takeaway: Use `==` for value equality, `===` for identity.
Trap: `===` doesn’t exist for structs.

cards.title: ARC basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ARC frees an object when its strong reference count hits zero.
Takeaway: Memory is automatic, but ownership still matters.
Trap: Strong reference cycles prevent deallocation.

cards.title: Strong references default
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: References are strong by default.
Takeaway: They keep objects alive.
Trap: Two objects holding each other strongly = memory leak.

cards.title: Weak references
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `weak` does not increase retain count and becomes nil when deallocated.
Takeaway: Breaks retain cycles safely.
Trap: `weak` must be `var` and is always optional.

cards.title: Unowned references
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `unowned` doesn’t retain and is non-optional.
Takeaway: Use only when lifetime is guaranteed.
Trap: If the object deallocates, `unowned` access crashes.

cards.title: Delegate should be weak
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Delegates are usually `weak`.
Takeaway: Prevent VC leaks.
Trap: Protocol must be class-only (`AnyObject`) to use weak.

cards.title: Classes & ARC — Class-only protocols
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `protocol P: AnyObject {}` for weak delegates.
Takeaway: Enables weak references.
Trap: Without `AnyObject`, the compiler forbids `weak`.

cards.title: Closures can retain self
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Closures capture `self` strongly by default.
Takeaway: Use `[weak self]` for escaping closures.
Trap: Stored closures on `self` commonly create cycles.

cards.title: Retain cycle pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `self -> closure` and `closure -> self` is a cycle.
Takeaway: Break it with weak capture or different ownership.
Trap: Cycles leak silently—watch deinit.

cards.title: deinit is your leak check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `deinit` runs when an object is freed.
Takeaway: Add logs to verify screens deallocate.
Trap: If deinit never runs, you probably leaked the object.

cards.title: Init must set properties
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: An initializer must initialize all stored properties.
Takeaway: Swift enforces safety.
Trap: Using `self` before init completes is illegal.

cards.title: Designated vs convenience init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Designated init fully initializes; convenience calls another init.
Takeaway: Convenience is for shortcuts.
Trap: Don’t create init chains that never reach a designated init.

cards.title: Initializer rules (classes)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Designated init calls `super.init`; convenience calls `self.init`.
Takeaway: There are strict rules.
Trap: Violations cause compile-time errors.

cards.title: required init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `required` forces subclasses to implement an initializer.
Takeaway: Needed for protocols/frameworks.
Trap: Forgetting required in subclass breaks conformance.

cards.title: Override requires override
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `override` when overriding a superclass method.
Takeaway: Compiler protection.
Trap: Forgetting to call `super` in UIKit lifecycle methods can break behavior.

cards.title: final class
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `final` prevents subclassing.
Takeaway: Safer and sometimes faster.
Trap: Don’t mark final if you truly need inheritance.

cards.title: Inheritance is single
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift classes inherit from one superclass.
Takeaway: Use protocols for multiple behavior.
Trap: Overusing inheritance leads to fragile hierarchies.

cards.title: Polymorphism
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A base-typed reference can hold a subclass instance.
Takeaway: Overridden methods dispatch dynamically.
Trap: Downcasting is a smell—prefer protocols when possible.

cards.title: as? downcast
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `as?` for safe downcasting.
Takeaway: Avoid crashes.
Trap: `as!` is unsafe if you’re not 100% sure.

cards.title: Two-phase initialization
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Class init happens in two phases for safety.
Takeaway: Stored properties set before using self.
Trap: Calling methods that use self before init completes is forbidden.

cards.title: Property observers in init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `willSet/didSet` don’t run for initial values in init.
Takeaway: Observers are for changes after init.
Trap: Don’t rely on didSet to set up dependent state in init.

cards.title: lazy properties
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `lazy` properties compute on first access.
Takeaway: Saves work if unused.
Trap: `lazy` isn’t thread-safe by default.

cards.title: Static vs class methods
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `static` methods can’t be overridden; `class` methods can.
Takeaway: Choose based on inheritance needs.
Trap: Using `static` when subclass customization is required.

cards.title: Reference in collections
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Arrays of classes store references.
Takeaway: Copying the array doesn’t copy the objects.
Trap: Mutating an object affects all arrays pointing to it.

cards.title: Copying objects
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If you need a true copy, implement copy/clone.
Takeaway: Make copying explicit.
Trap: `b = a` is not a copy—just another reference.

cards.title: NSCopying
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `NSCopying` is used in Obj-C interop for copying.
Takeaway: Sometimes needed with Foundation APIs.
Trap: Copy semantics must be defined carefully.

cards.title: Equatable in classes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `==` for classes is not automatic unless you implement it.
Takeaway: Define value equality when needed.
Trap: People assume `==` means identity—it might not.

cards.title: Hashable in classes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If class is Hashable, hash must match equality.
Takeaway: Stable keys for sets/dicts.
Trap: Mutating hashed fields after insertion breaks lookups.

cards.title: Weak must be var
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `weak` can only be declared as `var`.
Takeaway: Because it can become nil.
Trap: `weak let` is invalid.

cards.title: Unowned can crash
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `unowned` assumes the reference outlives the holder.
Takeaway: Use for parent-child where parent always lives longer.
Trap: Wrong assumption = crash.

cards.title: Timer retain cycle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Timers often retain their target.
Takeaway: Invalidate timers on deinit/disappear.
Trap: A repeating timer can keep a VC alive forever.

cards.title: NotificationCenter observers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Remove observers when using older addObserver APIs.
Takeaway: Avoid leaks or callbacks after deinit.
Trap: Forgetting removeObserver leads to crashes/leaks in legacy code.

cards.title: Combine subscriptions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Subscriptions can capture self in `sink`.
Takeaway: Use weak self or store cancellables properly.
Trap: Retain cycles happen through stored cancellables + closures.

cards.title: Async Task capturing self
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tasks can capture self strongly.
Takeaway: Cancel tasks when leaving screens.
Trap: Background tasks can outlive UI and update stale state.

cards.title: Cancel tasks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep a reference to Task and cancel it when needed.
Takeaway: Better UX and fewer leaks.
Trap: Cancellation is cooperative—check for cancellation.

cards.title: UIKit VC lifecycle leak check
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A dismissed/popped VC should deallocate.
Takeaway: Verify with deinit logs.
Trap: Strong captures, timers, and notifications are common culprits.

cards.title: Singleton lifetime
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Singletons live for the app lifetime.
Takeaway: Fine for services, not for UI.
Trap: Storing view controllers in a singleton leaks them.

cards.title: Dependency injection via init
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inject dependencies through initializers.
Takeaway: Better testability and clearer ownership.
Trap: Global singletons hide dependencies and complicate testing.

cards.title: Autoreleasepool (rare)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `autoreleasepool {}` can reduce peaks for heavy Obj-C bridged work.
Takeaway: Useful for huge loops of images.
Trap: Don’t use without profiling—often unnecessary.

cards.title: Memory graph debugging
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use Xcode Memory Graph to find retain cycles.
Takeaway: Visualizes ownership.
Trap: Ignoring leaks leads to crashes on older devices.

cards.title: Strong self in closure scope
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `guard let self else { return }` makes self strong for the block.
Takeaway: Prevents self disappearing mid-use.
Trap: Still don’t store that closure on self unless captured weakly.

cards.title: weak self + optional chaining
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `self?.do()` is safe but may hide missing work.
Takeaway: Use guard self when work must happen.
Trap: Silently skipping logic creates bugs.

cards.title: Retain cycle: parent/child
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Parent strongly holds child; child should weakly reference parent.
Takeaway: Break cycles.
Trap: If both are weak, objects may deallocate unexpectedly.

cards.title: Retain cycle: closures as properties
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stored closures on an object can create cycles.
Takeaway: Break with weak capture.
Trap: Even small closures can leak if stored.

cards.title: Retain cycle: delegate not weak
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Strong delegate references leak.
Takeaway: Delegates should almost always be weak.
Trap: Forgetting `AnyObject` makes weak impossible.

cards.title: ARC and value types
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ARC applies to reference types (classes), not structs/enums.
Takeaway: Value types deallocate naturally.
Trap: Structs can still hold class references that ARC manages.

cards.title: Deinit order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Subclass deinit runs before superclass deinit.
Takeaway: Cleanup order matters.
Trap: Don’t depend on superclass resources after it’s cleaned up.

cards.title: Property ownership checklist
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Decide who owns what: strong for ownership, weak for back-references.
Takeaway: Clear mental model.
Trap: “Everything strong” leads to leaks.

cards.title: When to use class
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use classes for identity, shared mutable state, UIKit objects.
Takeaway: Otherwise prefer structs.
Trap: Choosing class by habit increases bug surface.

cards.title: Reference equality is not value equality
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Two different objects can be equal by value.
Takeaway: Decide what equality means.
Trap: Using identity checks for value semantics is wrong.

cards.title: Thread-safety
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Classes with shared mutable state need synchronization.
Takeaway: Consider actors/locks.
Trap: Data races are intermittent and hard to reproduce.

cards.title: Weak collections need wrappers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: You can’t have `Array<weak T>`.
Takeaway: Use a WeakBox wrapper.
Trap: Forgetting cleanup leaves dead references.

cards.title: UIView/VC capture
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Capturing a VC in a long-lived closure often leaks it.
Takeaway: Use weak captures.
Trap: Networking completion handlers are common leak sources.

cards.title: Designated init must call super
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Subclass designated init must call `super.init`.
Takeaway: Proper initialization.
Trap: Calling instance methods before `super.init` is not allowed.

cards.title: Convenience init must call self
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Convenience init must delegate to another init in same class.
Takeaway: Shortcuts only.
Trap: Calling super from convenience directly violates rules.

cards.title: required + convenience
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A required initializer can be convenience.
Takeaway: Allowed when it delegates properly.
Trap: Be consistent across subclasses.

cards.title: Avoid Massive View Controllers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep VC thin; move logic to services/view models.
Takeaway: Easier testing and maintenance.
Trap: Dumping everything into VC creates unfixable code.

cards.title: Memory checklist for screens
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: weak delegate, weak self in callbacks, invalidate timers, cancel tasks.
Takeaway: Most leaks come from these.
Trap: Fixing leaks late is expensive.

modules.title: 8. Protocols & Generics
modules.moduleDescription: Protocol-oriented Swift, generics, constraints, existentials, and practical patterns.

cards.title: Protocols define contracts
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A protocol describes capabilities, not storage.
Takeaway: Use protocols to decouple code.
Trap: Don’t use protocols as “base classes”.

cards.title: Conformance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A type conforms by implementing requirements.
Takeaway: Compiler enforces the contract.
Trap: Missing a requirement is a compile-time error.

cards.title: Property requirements
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocols can require properties with `{ get }` or `{ get set }`.
Takeaway: Control mutability expectations.
Trap: `{ get set }` requires `var` in value types.

cards.title: Method requirements
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocol methods must match labels and types.
Takeaway: Labels are part of the signature.
Trap: Changing labels breaks conformance.

cards.title: Mutating requirement
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `mutating` in protocol requirements for value-type mutation.
Takeaway: Structs/enums can conform correctly.
Trap: Forgetting `mutating` makes conforming impossible for value types.

cards.title: Initializer requirements
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocols can require `init`.
Takeaway: Classes must mark it `required`.
Trap: Forgetting `required` breaks subclass conformance.

cards.title: Protocol inheritance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocols can inherit from other protocols.
Takeaway: Compose capabilities.
Trap: Deep protocol hierarchies reduce clarity.

cards.title: Protocols & Generics — Class-only protocols
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `protocol P: AnyObject` restricts to classes.
Takeaway: Enables weak delegates.
Trap: Structs/enums can’t conform.

cards.title: Protocol composition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `P & Q` to require multiple protocols.
Takeaway: Flexible APIs.
Trap: Too many composed protocols becomes unreadable.

cards.title: Extensions add behavior
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Extensions add methods/computed properties.
Takeaway: Organize code by feature.
Trap: Extensions can’t add stored properties.

cards.title: Default implementations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocol extensions can provide defaults.
Takeaway: Less boilerplate.
Trap: Default methods may dispatch statically if not requirements.

cards.title: Static dispatch trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Methods only in protocol extensions may be statically dispatched.
Takeaway: Call-site type matters.
Trap: Calling through `any P` may not use your “override-like” behavior.

cards.title: Requirement vs extension method
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Put methods in requirements if you need dynamic dispatch.
Takeaway: Make intent explicit.
Trap: “Why didn’t my implementation run?”—it wasn’t a requirement.

cards.title: Existentials: any P
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `any P` is an existential (type-erased container).
Takeaway: Flexible but less type info.
Trap: Existentials can be slower and have limitations.

cards.title: Generics: T: P
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `T: P` keeps the concrete type at compile time.
Takeaway: Often faster and more expressive.
Trap: Don’t use `any P` when a generic fits.

cards.title: Existential limitations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocols with associated types or `Self` requirements are limited as existentials.
Takeaway: You may need type erasure.
Trap: “Protocol can only be used as a generic constraint” errors.

cards.title: associatedtype
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `associatedtype` makes a protocol generic-like.
Takeaway: Powers `Sequence`/`Collection`.
Trap: You can’t store `any P` easily when P has associatedtype.

cards.title: Self requirements
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Methods returning `Self` restrict existential use.
Takeaway: Great for fluent APIs.
Trap: Hard to use with `any P` containers.

cards.title: Opaque types: some P
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `some P` returns a specific hidden type.
Takeaway: Keeps performance and type safety.
Trap: `some P` is not “any conformer”; it’s one concrete type.

cards.title: Generics basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Generics enable reusable code: `struct Box<T>`.
Takeaway: Type-safe reuse.
Trap: Generics are not the same as `Any`.

cards.title: Protocols & Generics — Generic constraints
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Add constraints: `T: Comparable`.
Takeaway: Enables operations like `<`.
Trap: Without constraints, you can’t call protocol methods.

cards.title: where clauses
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `where` for precise constraints.
Takeaway: `where T.Element: Hashable`.
Trap: Overly complex where clauses hurt readability.

cards.title: Protocols & Generics — Same-type constraints
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tie types together: `where T.Element == Int`.
Takeaway: Specialized behavior.
Trap: You may accidentally block legitimate use cases.

cards.title: Conditional conformance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Types can conform conditionally: `extension Array: Equatable where Element: Equatable`.
Takeaway: Powerful composition.
Trap: Debugging conditional conformance can be tricky.

cards.title: Protocol extensions with where
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide defaults only for certain Self types.
Takeaway: `extension P where Self: UIViewController`.
Trap: Hidden behavior can surprise readers.

cards.title: Type erasure concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Type erasure hides concrete types behind a wrapper.
Takeaway: Store heterogeneous conformers.
Trap: More complexity—use only when needed.

cards.title: AnySequence
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `AnySequence` erases a sequence type.
Takeaway: Stable return types in APIs.
Trap: Sometimes returning a concrete type is simpler.

cards.title: AnyHashable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `AnyHashable` erases Hashable types.
Takeaway: Useful for heterogeneous keys.
Trap: Prefer homogeneous key types when possible.

cards.title: AnyView
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `AnyView` erases SwiftUI view type.
Takeaway: Useful for conditional branches.
Trap: Can reduce performance and diagnostics.

cards.title: Protocol-oriented programming
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Swift often favors protocols + extensions.
Takeaway: Composition over inheritance.
Trap: “Protocol soup” can be harder than a simple class.

cards.title: Marker protocols
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Empty protocols can tag types.
Takeaway: Useful for constraints.
Trap: Don’t create markers without a real use.

cards.title: Dependency injection via protocol
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Depend on protocols, not concrete types.
Takeaway: Easier testing and swapping implementations.
Trap: Don’t over-abstract trivial dependencies.

cards.title: Mocking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mocks conform to the same protocol.
Takeaway: Test without network/db.
Trap: Mocks should mimic real behavior enough to be meaningful.

cards.title: Retroactive modeling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Extend existing types to conform to protocols.
Takeaway: Adds behavior without subclassing.
Trap: Cross-module conformance conflicts can happen.

cards.title: Conformance conflicts
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A type can’t conform to the same protocol twice.
Takeaway: Keep conformance in one place.
Trap: Duplicate extensions across modules cause build errors.

cards.title: Performance: generics vs existentials
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Generics are often faster than `any P`.
Takeaway: Prefer generics in hot paths.
Trap: Premature optimization—measure if it matters.

cards.title: Dynamic dispatch basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocol requirements dispatch via witness tables.
Takeaway: Efficient polymorphism.
Trap: Extension-only methods may behave differently.

cards.title: Designing small protocols
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer small, focused protocols.
Takeaway: Easier composition.
Trap: “God protocols” become unimplementable.

cards.title: Protocol composition vs inheritance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Composition (`P & Q`) avoids deep inheritance trees.
Takeaway: Flexible APIs.
Trap: Over-composing becomes unreadable.

cards.title: Generics in functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `func swapTwo<T>(_ a: inout T, _ b: inout T)`.
Takeaway: One function for many types.
Trap: Don’t forget `inout` and `&` at call sites.

cards.title: Generic algorithms on Collection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Write utilities on `Collection` protocols.
Takeaway: Works for arrays, slices, sets.
Trap: Don’t require Array unless you need random access.

cards.title: Sequence vs Collection
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Collection has stable indices and often O(1) count.
Takeaway: Choose based on needs.
Trap: Assuming Sequence supports efficient indexing.

cards.title: Invariance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Array<Dog>` is not `Array<Animal>`.
Takeaway: Generic types are usually invariant.
Trap: Expecting covariance like in some other languages.

cards.title: Typealias is not a new type
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `typealias` is just an alias.
Takeaway: Improves readability.
Trap: It doesn’t add safety or constraints.

cards.title: Opaque result in SwiftUI
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SwiftUI uses `some View` everywhere.
Takeaway: Strong types, good performance.
Trap: Returning different view types needs builders or erasure.

cards.title: @ViewBuilder concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: View builders allow multiple child views in a closure.
Takeaway: Great for conditional UI.
Trap: Don’t hide complex business logic in builders.

cards.title: Return different views
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Without builders, both branches must match types.
Takeaway: Use `Group`, `@ViewBuilder`, or `AnyView`.
Trap: Overusing `AnyView` can hurt performance.

cards.title: Protocol with associatedtype example
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `protocol Storage { associatedtype Item }`.
Takeaway: Strongly typed storage.
Trap: You can’t store `any Storage` directly without erasure.

cards.title: Prefer generics over Any
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use generics to keep types.
Takeaway: Better compiler help.
Trap: `Any` often causes runtime casts and crashes.

cards.title: Any vs any P
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Any` is any type; `any P` is any type conforming to P.
Takeaway: `any P` is safer.
Trap: Still loses concrete type information.

cards.title: Self in protocol extensions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Extension constraints can use `Self`.
Takeaway: Powerful specialization.
Trap: Harder to discover in code search.

cards.title: Type erasure pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `AnyX` often stores a base value + closures.
Takeaway: Makes associatedtype protocols storable.
Trap: Closures can capture strongly—watch memory.

cards.title: Stability of public APIs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocols help keep APIs stable while changing implementations.
Takeaway: Safer refactors.
Trap: Over-general APIs become hard to evolve.

cards.title: When to use existentials
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `any P` when you need heterogeneity.
Takeaway: Great for plugin-style lists.
Trap: Avoid `any P` when generics provide better type safety.

cards.title: When to use type erasure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use type erasure when associatedtype protocols must be stored.
Takeaway: It’s a tool, not default.
Trap: Extra abstraction can complicate debugging.

cards.title: Protocol + enum
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Enums can conform to protocols too.
Takeaway: State machines can be polymorphic.
Trap: Don’t over-abstract state.

cards.title: Protocol-based delegates
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UIKit uses delegate protocols everywhere.
Takeaway: Learn them well.
Trap: Retain cycles if delegates aren’t weak.

cards.title: Generic constraints readability
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer readable constraints.
Takeaway: Split complex constraints into helper types.
Trap: One giant where clause is hard to maintain.

cards.title: Associated types and collections
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Associated types enable generic collections.
Takeaway: Strong typing.
Trap: Existentials lose that strong typing.

cards.title: Comparator generic
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use constraints for sorting: `T: Comparable`.
Takeaway: Enables default ordering.
Trap: Sorting without a stable rule yields inconsistent UI.

cards.title: Equatable conditional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many stdlib types conform conditionally.
Takeaway: Works automatically when elements do.
Trap: Custom types may need explicit conformance.

cards.title: SwiftUI AnyView caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: AnyView solves type problems but can cost performance.
Takeaway: Use only when needed.
Trap: “AnyView everywhere” kills compile-time help.

cards.title: Testability via protocols
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protocols make mocking easy.
Takeaway: Better unit tests.
Trap: Mocks must reflect real edge cases.

cards.title: Avoid over-abstraction
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start concrete, extract protocols when you feel pain.
Takeaway: YAGNI.
Trap: Abstracting too early slows development.

modules.title: 9. Concurrency
modules.moduleDescription: async/await, Task, actors, cancellation, and avoiding data races.

cards.title: Why concurrency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Concurrency keeps apps responsive by avoiding main-thread blocking.
Takeaway: Do heavy work off the UI thread.
Trap: “Concurrent” doesn’t automatically mean “faster”.

cards.title: async/await idea
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `async` functions can suspend; `await` marks suspension points.
Takeaway: Code reads linearly.
Trap: `await` doesn’t mean “new thread”—it’s a suspension point.

cards.title: Calling async
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Calling an async function requires `await`.
Takeaway: Makes waiting visible.
Trap: Forgetting `await` is a compile-time error.

cards.title: async throws
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `async throws` needs `try await` at call sites.
Takeaway: Clear error and suspension points.
Trap: Handle errors and cancellation separately.

cards.title: Task basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Task { ... }` starts async work from sync context.
Takeaway: Great for button taps and lifecycle hooks.
Trap: Tasks can capture `self` strongly—watch memory.

cards.title: Task value
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Task` can return a value: `let t = Task { ... }`.
Takeaway: Use `await t.value`.
Trap: For throwing tasks use `try await t.value`.

cards.title: Task priority
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tasks have priorities as scheduling hints.
Takeaway: Useful for UI vs background work.
Trap: Priority is not a guarantee—don’t rely on it for correctness.

cards.title: Task.detached caution
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Task.detached` does not inherit actor context.
Takeaway: Use it rarely.
Trap: Touching UI or actor-isolated state from detached can break safety.

cards.title: Structured concurrency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer structured tasks that live within a scope.
Takeaway: Automatic lifetime and cancellation.
Trap: Detached “fire-and-forget” tasks leak work and bugs.

cards.title: async let
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `async let` starts child tasks concurrently.
Takeaway: Await later: `let r = await x`.
Trap: Forgetting to await can still force waiting at scope exit.

cards.title: async let + try
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: With throwing functions, `try` happens when awaiting.
Takeaway: `async let x = f()` then `try await x`.
Trap: Trying to write `async let x = try f()` is invalid.

cards.title: TaskGroup basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `withTaskGroup` runs many tasks concurrently.
Takeaway: Gather results efficiently.
Trap: Result order is not guaranteed.

cards.title: ThrowingTaskGroup
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `withThrowingTaskGroup` propagates errors.
Takeaway: Fail fast when needed.
Trap: One failure can cancel the rest—design for partial results.

cards.title: Cancellation is cooperative
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cancellation stops work only if code checks for it.
Takeaway: Design tasks to be cancel-aware.
Trap: Assuming cancel immediately stops CPU work.

cards.title: Task.isCancelled
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Check `Task.isCancelled` in long loops.
Takeaway: Exit early.
Trap: Not checking causes wasted CPU/battery.

cards.title: Task.checkCancellation()
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try Task.checkCancellation()` throws `CancellationError`.
Takeaway: Standard cancellation path.
Trap: Don’t treat cancellation as a normal failure.

cards.title: CancellationError handling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Handle cancellation separately from real errors.
Takeaway: User canceled ≠ failure.
Trap: Showing error alerts when user just navigated back.

cards.title: Task.sleep
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Task.sleep` suspends without blocking a thread.
Takeaway: Use for delays/backoff.
Trap: Don’t use `Thread.sleep` in async code—it blocks.

cards.title: Task.yield
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `await Task.yield()` lets other tasks run.
Takeaway: Helps fairness in long computations.
Trap: Not a substitute for proper architecture.

cards.title: MainActor concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UI updates must happen on the main actor.
Takeaway: Use `@MainActor` for UI-facing code.
Trap: Heavy work on MainActor causes jank.

cards.title: MainActor.run
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `await MainActor.run { ... }` hops to main.
Takeaway: Update UI safely.
Trap: Keep the block small—no networking/parsing.

cards.title: Concurrency — @MainActor ViewModel
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many view models are `@MainActor`.
Takeaway: Safe state updates.
Trap: Offload heavy work to background tasks.

cards.title: Actors basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Actors protect mutable state from data races.
Takeaway: Serialize access to state.
Trap: Actors don’t protect external shared references you pass out.

cards.title: Actor isolation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Accessing actor state from outside requires `await`.
Takeaway: Compiler enforces safety.
Trap: Don’t circumvent with `nonisolated` unless safe.

cards.title: nonisolated
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `nonisolated` methods don’t touch actor-isolated state.
Takeaway: Callable without await.
Trap: Touching isolated state inside nonisolated is illegal.

cards.title: Reentrancy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Actors can be re-entered at await points.
Takeaway: State may change between awaits.
Trap: Don’t assume invariants hold across an `await`.

cards.title: Actor invariants
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Maintain invariants without awaiting mid-update.
Takeaway: Update state before awaiting.
Trap: “Set flag, await, use flag” can break.

cards.title: Sendable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Sendable` means values are safe to transfer between tasks.
Takeaway: Value types are often Sendable.
Trap: Classes are usually not Sendable by default.

cards.title: @unchecked Sendable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@unchecked Sendable` bypasses compiler checks.
Takeaway: Only when you truly guarantee safety.
Trap: It can hide real race bugs.

cards.title: Data races
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A data race is concurrent unsynchronized access.
Takeaway: Prevent with actors/locks.
Trap: Race bugs are intermittent and hard to reproduce.

cards.title: Locks vs actors
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Locks can work, actors are often safer in Swift.
Takeaway: Prefer actors for state.
Trap: Locks can deadlock if misused.

cards.title: Deadlock example
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Synchronous waits on main thread can deadlock.
Takeaway: Avoid `dispatchSync` to main.
Trap: “Works sometimes” is a warning sign.

cards.title: AsyncSequence
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `for await x in stream` consumes async sequences.
Takeaway: Streams of values over time.
Trap: For throwing streams use `for try await`.

cards.title: AsyncStream
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `AsyncStream` bridges callbacks to async sequences.
Takeaway: Modernize delegate/callback APIs.
Trap: Forgetting to finish the stream can leak work.

cards.title: Buffering policy
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Streams can buffer.
Takeaway: Control memory.
Trap: Unlimited buffering can grow memory unbounded.

cards.title: Continuations
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Continuations bridge callback -> async.
Takeaway: Use checked continuations.
Trap: Must resume exactly once.

cards.title: Resume exactly once
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Continuations must be resumed once.
Takeaway: Avoid hangs and crashes.
Trap: Resume twice is a bug; never resume hangs forever.

cards.title: URLSession async
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: URLSession offers async APIs like `data(from:)`.
Takeaway: Cleaner networking.
Trap: It doesn’t throw for HTTP 404—check status codes.

cards.title: HTTP status handling
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Treat non-2xx as errors.
Takeaway: Validate `HTTPURLResponse.statusCode`.
Trap: Decoding error payload as success causes confusing bugs.

cards.title: Retry with backoff
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Retry transient failures with backoff.
Takeaway: More resilient apps.
Trap: Infinite retries drain battery and spam servers.

cards.title: Timeout pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Implement timeouts with Task groups or race vs `Task.sleep`.
Takeaway: Avoid infinite waits.
Trap: Always cancel the losing task.

cards.title: Debounce user input
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Debounce search queries.
Takeaway: Fewer requests and better UX.
Trap: Without canceling old tasks, results arrive out of order.

cards.title: Concurrency — Out-of-order responses
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Async results can arrive in any order.
Takeaway: Track request tokens/IDs.
Trap: Old responses overwriting newer state is common.

cards.title: Cancel on disappear
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cancel in-flight tasks when a screen disappears.
Takeaway: Save resources.
Trap: Updating UI after dismiss leads to warnings/crashes.

cards.title: Detached lifetime
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Detached tasks can outlive the UI.
Takeaway: Use only for truly independent work.
Trap: Side effects after user leaves the screen.

cards.title: Bridging callback APIs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Wrap callback APIs with continuations.
Takeaway: Consistent async style.
Trap: Handle all callback paths (success/failure/cancel).

cards.title: Bridging delegates
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Turn delegate events into AsyncStream.
Takeaway: Stream-based consumption.
Trap: Ensure stream finishes on deinit.

cards.title: Main thread blocking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: CPU-heavy loops on main freeze UI.
Takeaway: Move work off main.
Trap: “It’s fast on my phone” isn’t a guarantee.

cards.title: Priority inversion
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: High-priority tasks waiting on low-priority work can slow UI.
Takeaway: Avoid long critical sections.
Trap: Priorities are hints—design for correctness first.

cards.title: TaskLocal concept
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Task-local values can carry context.
Takeaway: Advanced feature.
Trap: Overuse makes debugging harder.

cards.title: Await points change state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Treat every `await` as a possible interleaving point.
Takeaway: Re-check assumptions after awaiting.
Trap: Bugs come from assuming state is unchanged.

cards.title: Actor for cache
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use an actor for caches/shared stores.
Takeaway: Race-free access.
Trap: Keep cached values small and bounded.

cards.title: Memory growth in caches
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Caches need eviction/limits.
Takeaway: Control memory.
Trap: Unbounded caches cause OOM crashes.

cards.title: Async init workaround
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Initializers can’t be async in most cases.
Takeaway: Use `static func create() async` or `load()`.
Trap: Doing async work in init leads to awkward hacks.

cards.title: Async property getters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Async computed properties exist but are rare.
Takeaway: Prefer async methods.
Trap: Async properties can hide expensive work behind property syntax.

cards.title: Testing concurrency
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Test async code with async XCTest and controlled schedulers.
Takeaway: Deterministic tests.
Trap: Flaky tests often come from timing assumptions.

cards.title: Cancellation in loops
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In loops, check for cancellation regularly.
Takeaway: Responsive cancellation.
Trap: Long CPU loops without checks ignore cancellation.

cards.title: Don’t swallow cancellation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don’t convert cancellation into a generic error.
Takeaway: Let cancellation propagate.
Trap: Treating cancel as failure breaks UX.

cards.title: Race vs async let
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For a few parallel tasks, use `async let`.
Takeaway: Simple and structured.
Trap: For dynamic counts, use TaskGroup instead.

cards.title: TaskGroup cancellation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cancel remaining tasks when one fails if appropriate.
Takeaway: Save work.
Trap: Decide if partial results are acceptable.

cards.title: MainActor in SwiftUI
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SwiftUI state updates should happen on main.
Takeaway: Use MainActor for UI state.
Trap: Updating @State from background can warn or misbehave.

cards.title: Multiple taps create tasks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Buttons can start multiple Tasks.
Takeaway: Disable or debounce while loading.
Trap: Duplicate in-flight tasks cause inconsistent state.

cards.title: Progress state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Model loading state explicitly.
Takeaway: Disable UI, show progress.
Trap: Multiple boolean flags create invalid combinations.

cards.title: AsyncSequence backpressure
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Streams can outpace consumers.
Takeaway: Use buffering policy or drop strategy.
Trap: Unbounded buffering increases memory.

cards.title: Instrument performance
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Measure with Instruments before optimizing.
Takeaway: Fix real bottlenecks.
Trap: Guessing wastes time.

cards.title: Concurrency — Energy impact
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Frequent wakeups/animations drain battery.
Takeaway: Minimize background work.
Trap: Infinite polling tasks are expensive.

cards.title: Best practice: structured first
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start with structured concurrency and actors.
Takeaway: Safer default.
Trap: Detached tasks are easy to misuse.

cards.title: Error handling split
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Handle network errors, decoding errors, and cancellation differently.
Takeaway: Better UX.
Trap: One catch-all “Something went wrong” hides useful info.

modules.title: 10. Networking + Codable + Persistence
modules.moduleDescription: URLSession, status codes, Codable JSON, caching, and basic persistence.

cards.title: Networking mindset
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Networks fail—design for errors and retries.
Takeaway: Assume requests can fail at any time.
Trap: “Works on my Wi‑Fi” is not production reality.

cards.title: URL vs String
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `URL`/`URLComponents` over manual string building.
Takeaway: Correct encoding and fewer bugs.
Trap: Hand-built query strings break on spaces/emoji.

cards.title: URL(string:) is optional
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `URL(string:)` returns `URL?`.
Takeaway: Validate URLs before use.
Trap: Force unwrapping invalid URLs crashes.

cards.title: URLComponents
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `URLComponents` + `URLQueryItem` for query params.
Takeaway: Safe percent-encoding.
Trap: `components.url` can be nil—handle it.

cards.title: HTTP methods
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: GET reads, POST creates, PUT updates, DELETE removes.
Takeaway: Match intent.
Trap: Sending bodies with GET is unreliable.

cards.title: URLRequest basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `URLRequest` to set method/headers/body.
Takeaway: More control than `data(from:)`.
Trap: Forgetting `httpMethod` means GET by default.

cards.title: Headers
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use headers like `Content-Type` and `Authorization`.
Takeaway: Server understands payload and auth.
Trap: Wrong Content-Type breaks server parsing.

cards.title: Bearer auth
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is common.
Takeaway: Standard pattern.
Trap: Never hardcode tokens in the app.

cards.title: Timeouts
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set request timeouts.
Takeaway: Avoid infinite hangs.
Trap: Too-short timeouts cause false failures.

cards.title: URLSession shared
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `URLSession.shared` is fine for simple cases.
Takeaway: Start simple.
Trap: For advanced needs, configure your own session.

cards.title: Async URLSession
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `try await session.data(for: request)`.
Takeaway: Modern linear style.
Trap: It doesn’t automatically treat non-2xx as errors.

cards.title: HTTPURLResponse
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cast response to `HTTPURLResponse` to read status.
Takeaway: Validate `statusCode`.
Trap: Ignoring status leads to decoding error bodies as success.

cards.title: 2xx success
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Treat 200–299 as success by default.
Takeaway: Standard HTTP semantics.
Trap: 204 No Content has empty body—don’t decode JSON.

cards.title: 204 No Content
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Handle 204 separately.
Takeaway: Success without a payload.
Trap: Decoding empty Data throws DecodingError.

cards.title: Error mapping
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Map errors into your own `NetworkError` enum.
Takeaway: Cleaner UI messaging.
Trap: Surfacing raw errors to users is confusing.

cards.title: Transient vs permanent errors
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Retry only transient issues (timeouts, 5xx).
Takeaway: Smarter retry behavior.
Trap: Retrying 4xx usually wastes time.

cards.title: Backoff
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use exponential backoff for retries.
Takeaway: Less server load.
Trap: Rapid retries can trigger rate limits.

cards.title: Rate limits 429
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Handle 429 and respect `Retry-After` when present.
Takeaway: Avoid bans.
Trap: Retrying immediately makes it worse.

cards.title: Cancellation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Task cancellation cancels URLSession requests.
Takeaway: Save bandwidth.
Trap: Don’t show error alerts for cancellation.

cards.title: JSON basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: JSON types: object, array, string, number, bool, null.
Takeaway: Match models to payload.
Trap: Numbers might be Int or Double depending on server.

cards.title: Codable
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Codable` = Encodable + Decodable.
Takeaway: Standard Swift JSON mapping.
Trap: Type mismatches cause decode failures.

cards.title: Decode JSON
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try JSONDecoder().decode(Model.self, from: data)`.
Takeaway: The core pattern.
Trap: Always handle decoding errors.

cards.title: Decode array top-level
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: JSON can be a top-level array.
Takeaway: Decode `[Model].self`.
Trap: Decoding an object when payload is an array fails.

cards.title: Networking + Codable + Persistence — CodingKeys
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `CodingKeys` to map server keys.
Takeaway: snake_case to camelCase.
Trap: Missing mapping breaks decode for non-optional properties.

cards.title: convertFromSnakeCase
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `decoder.keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase`.
Takeaway: Less boilerplate.
Trap: It’s not perfect for all edge cases.

cards.title: Date decoding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set `dateDecodingStrategy`.
Takeaway: `.iso8601` is common.
Trap: Servers often use custom formats—test real data.

cards.title: Encode JSON
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `try JSONEncoder().encode(model)`.
Takeaway: Build request bodies.
Trap: Encoder date strategy must match server expectations.

cards.title: Content-Type application/json
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Set `Content-Type: application/json` for JSON bodies.
Takeaway: Server parses correctly.
Trap: Missing header can cause 400 errors.

cards.title: HTTP body pitfalls
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: GET requests should not rely on `httpBody`.
Takeaway: Use query parameters.
Trap: Some servers ignore GET bodies entirely.

cards.title: DecodingError debugging
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Catch `DecodingError` and inspect context.
Takeaway: Fast root cause.
Trap: `try?` hides the error details.

cards.title: Log payloads safely
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Log raw JSON only in debug and without secrets.
Takeaway: Debug faster.
Trap: Logging tokens/PII is a security risk.

cards.title: Nullable fields
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If server can send null, model property should be optional.
Takeaway: Decode succeeds.
Trap: Making everything optional weakens guarantees.

cards.title: Numbers as strings
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Some APIs send numbers as strings.
Takeaway: Use custom decoding when needed.
Trap: Assuming `Int` always decodes from JSON number.

cards.title: Enum raw values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `enum Status: String, Codable` is easy.
Takeaway: Clean mapping.
Trap: Unknown values can break decoding.

cards.title: Networking + Codable + Persistence — Unknown enum case
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Add a fallback case via custom decode.
Takeaway: Forward compatible.
Trap: Silently mapping everything to `.unknown` can hide server changes.

cards.title: Pagination
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Many APIs paginate results.
Takeaway: Track page/limit and reset on new searches.
Trap: Forgetting to reset page causes weird UX.

cards.title: Networking + Codable + Persistence — Out-of-order responses
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Responses can arrive out of order.
Takeaway: Use request IDs or latest-only logic.
Trap: Stale responses overwriting fresh UI is common.

cards.title: Caching basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cache when it improves UX and saves bandwidth.
Takeaway: Faster startup.
Trap: Cache needs invalidation (TTL/ETag).

cards.title: URLCache
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: URLSession can use URLCache.
Takeaway: Leverage HTTP caching headers.
Trap: No headers = no caching benefit.

cards.title: ETag / 304
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ETag + 304 Not Modified saves bandwidth.
Takeaway: Efficient refresh.
Trap: Only works if server supports it.

cards.title: Persistence reason
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Persist key data for offline and quick launch.
Takeaway: Better UX.
Trap: Storing everything leads to bloat and migration pain.

cards.title: UserDefaults use
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use UserDefaults for small settings/flags.
Takeaway: Simple persistence.
Trap: Don’t store big JSON or images there.

cards.title: FileManager cache
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Store cached data in the Caches directory.
Takeaway: System may purge it.
Trap: Putting cache in Documents triggers backups and bloat.

cards.title: Documents directory
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use Documents for user-created content.
Takeaway: Backed up content.
Trap: Storing ephemeral cache here is wrong.

cards.title: Keychain
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Store secrets (tokens) in Keychain.
Takeaway: Safer than UserDefaults.
Trap: Rolling your own crypto storage is risky.

cards.title: Atomic writes
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Write files atomically to avoid corruption.
Takeaway: Safer disk persistence.
Trap: Crashes during writes can leave partial files.

cards.title: Disk errors
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Disk reads/writes can fail.
Takeaway: Handle IO errors.
Trap: `try?` hides real storage issues.

cards.title: No disk space
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Devices can run out of space.
Takeaway: Fail gracefully.
Trap: Assuming “there is always space” causes crashes.

cards.title: Migration versioning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Version stored formats.
Takeaway: Future-proof persistence.
Trap: Changing models without migration breaks old installs.

cards.title: Offline-first pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Show cached data first, then refresh.
Takeaway: Fast UI.
Trap: Clearly indicate loading/refresh to avoid confusion.

cards.title: Repository layer
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use a Repository to decide network vs cache.
Takeaway: Cleaner architecture.
Trap: Putting networking code directly in views/controllers.

cards.title: DTO vs domain model
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Separate API DTOs from app domain models.
Takeaway: Decouple UI from API changes.
Trap: Reusing DTOs everywhere makes refactors painful.

cards.title: Mapping functions
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `toDomain()` mapping.
Takeaway: Clear boundaries.
Trap: Forgetting to update mapping after API changes.

cards.title: Reachability is a hint
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Network reachability isn’t a guarantee.
Takeaway: Still handle request failures.
Trap: Skipping requests because “offline” can be wrong.

cards.title: ATS / HTTPS
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use HTTPS; App Transport Security enforces safety.
Takeaway: Better security.
Trap: Adding ATS exceptions without reason is risky.

cards.title: Certificate pinning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pinning increases security but adds maintenance.
Takeaway: Consider for high-security apps.
Trap: Pins expire—plan rotations.

cards.title: Avoid logging secrets
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Never log auth headers or tokens.
Takeaway: Security hygiene.
Trap: Debug logs can end up in crash reports.

cards.title: Unit test decoding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Test decode with fixture JSON.
Takeaway: Catch breaking changes early.
Trap: Only testing “happy path” payloads.

cards.title: Mock networking
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mock URLSession/URLProtocol for tests.
Takeaway: Fast deterministic tests.
Trap: Tests that hit real servers are flaky.

cards.title: Inject URLSession
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Inject session as a dependency.
Takeaway: Testable networking.
Trap: Hardcoding `URLSession.shared` everywhere.

cards.title: Combine vs async
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: async/await is great for requests; streams may use Combine/AsyncSequence.
Takeaway: Choose the right tool.
Trap: Mixing paradigms randomly adds complexity.

cards.title: Decode off main
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Decode large JSON off the main thread.
Takeaway: Smooth UI.
Trap: Doing heavy decode on main causes jank.

cards.title: Update UI on main
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UI updates must happen on main.
Takeaway: Use MainActor.
Trap: Updating UI from background leads to warnings/crashes.

cards.title: Batch requests
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Batch network calls when possible.
Takeaway: Fewer requests.
Trap: One request per cell leads to poor performance.

cards.title: Error UX
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Show actionable, friendly errors.
Takeaway: Better retention.
Trap: Showing raw technical errors to users.

cards.title: Retry button
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide a retry path for recoverable failures.
Takeaway: Users can self-recover.
Trap: Auto-retrying forever without user control.

modules.title: 11. SwiftUI Fundamentals
modules.moduleDescription: Views, modifiers, stacks, lists, navigation primitives, and building screens declaratively.

cards.title: SwiftUI is declarative
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Describe what UI should be, not how to draw it.
Takeaway: UI is a function of state.
Trap: Thinking in UIKit “imperative” steps leads to fighting SwiftUI.

cards.title: View is a value
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SwiftUI views are value types.
Takeaway: They’re cheap to create and compose.
Trap: Trying to store and mutate a view instance directly.

cards.title: body returns some View
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `var body: some View` returns a view tree.
Takeaway: Compose small views.
Trap: Heavy work in body causes jank.

cards.title: Modifiers create new views
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Modifiers return new view values.
Takeaway: Chaining is normal.
Trap: Modifier order matters.

cards.title: Modifier order
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.padding().background()` differs from `.background().padding()`.
Takeaway: Think about size at each step.
Trap: “Why is my background small?”—order is wrong.

cards.title: Text basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Text` displays strings.
Takeaway: Use modifiers for style.
Trap: Don’t build huge text layouts with `+`—use interpolation.

cards.title: Image basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Image("asset")` uses assets; `Image(systemName:)` uses SF Symbols.
Takeaway: Know both.
Trap: Wrong names silently show nothing.

cards.title: SF Symbols
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Image(systemName:)` uses SF Symbols.
Takeaway: Scales and adapts well.
Trap: Not all symbols exist on all OS versions.

cards.title: Resizable images
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.resizable()` before scaling.
Takeaway: Combine with `.scaledToFit()` or `.scaledToFill()`.
Trap: Resizable without scaling can distort.

cards.title: scaledToFit vs fill
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Fit preserves all content; fill crops to fill bounds.
Takeaway: Pick based on design.
Trap: Fill needs clipping to avoid overflow.

cards.title: VStack/HStack
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use stacks for layout.
Takeaway: Simple composition.
Trap: Too many nested stacks can be hard to read—extract subviews.

cards.title: ZStack
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ZStack layers views.
Takeaway: Good for overlays.
Trap: Overusing ZStack when a background/overlay would do.

cards.title: Spacer
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Spacer takes flexible space.
Takeaway: Easy alignment.
Trap: Multiple spacers can create unexpected gaps.

cards.title: Alignment in stacks
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stacks have alignment parameters.
Takeaway: Align by leading/center/trailing.
Trap: Stack alignment is not the same as frame alignment.

cards.title: frame basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.frame(width:height:alignment:)` influences layout.
Takeaway: Use for constraints and alignment.
Trap: Overusing fixed sizes breaks Dynamic Type.

cards.title: SwiftUI Fundamentals — maxWidth .infinity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` expands to available width.
Takeaway: Combine with alignment for left/right.
Trap: In HStack it can steal space from siblings.

cards.title: padding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.padding()` adds spacing around a view.
Takeaway: Helps UI breathe.
Trap: Padding affects background size depending on modifier order.

cards.title: background
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.background(...)` draws behind a view.
Takeaway: Great for cards.
Trap: Background uses the view’s current size—order matters.

cards.title: overlay
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.overlay(...)` draws on top.
Takeaway: Borders, badges.
Trap: Overlay also depends on current view size.

cards.title: clipShape
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `clipShape` clips to a shape.
Takeaway: Use for rounded corners and avatars.
Trap: CornerRadius may not clip background as expected—clipShape is more explicit.

cards.title: foregroundStyle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer `foregroundStyle` for modern styling.
Takeaway: Works well with materials.
Trap: `foregroundColor` is fine but less flexible.

cards.title: Fonts
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.font(.title)` etc.
Takeaway: System fonts adapt to Dynamic Type.
Trap: Hardcoded fonts can break accessibility.

cards.title: Dynamic Type awareness
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SwiftUI adapts to user font size settings.
Takeaway: Test with larger text.
Trap: Fixed frames can truncate in large sizes.

cards.title: Button basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Button` runs an action closure.
Takeaway: Keep actions quick; start async work in a Task.
Trap: Doing heavy work directly in the action blocks UI.

cards.title: Button styles
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.buttonStyle(...)` for consistent UI.
Takeaway: System styles look native.
Trap: Over-custom styling can harm accessibility.

cards.title: Label
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Label` pairs text with an icon.
Takeaway: More semantic than HStack(Image+Text).
Trap: Manually rebuilding Label loses automatic behaviors.

cards.title: TextField basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: TextField needs a `Binding` to text.
Takeaway: Use `@State var text`.
Trap: Passing a plain String won’t update.

cards.title: SecureField
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SecureField hides input.
Takeaway: Use for passwords.
Trap: Don’t store secrets in plain text.

cards.title: Toggle
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Toggle binds to a Bool.
Takeaway: Use `@State`/`@Binding`.
Trap: If the value isn’t a binding, UI won’t change.

cards.title: Picker basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Picker binds to a selection.
Takeaway: Use tags.
Trap: Tags must match selection type exactly.

cards.title: Slider
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Slider binds to a Double.
Takeaway: Provide range and step.
Trap: Don’t treat slider values as Int without conversion.

cards.title: Form
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Form is great for settings-style UI.
Takeaway: iOS-native layout.
Trap: Form behavior differs across platforms—test.

cards.title: Section
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use Section inside Form/List.
Takeaway: Structure and headers.
Trap: Too many sections can feel heavy; group thoughtfully.

cards.title: List basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: List is for large scrolling collections.
Takeaway: Built-in performance behaviors.
Trap: Nesting List inside ScrollView causes conflicts.

cards.title: ForEach needs identity
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ForEach needs stable IDs.
Takeaway: Adopt Identifiable.
Trap: Using array indices as IDs breaks on insert/delete.

cards.title: Identifiable models
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use stable IDs for list diffing.
Takeaway: Smooth updates.
Trap: Generating new UUIDs each render causes constant re-creation.

cards.title: SwiftUI Fundamentals — NavigationStack
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `NavigationStack` for navigation.
Takeaway: Modern replacement for NavigationView.
Trap: NavigationLink outside NavigationStack won’t push.

cards.title: NavigationLink
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: NavigationLink triggers navigation.
Takeaway: Simple push UI.
Trap: Building heavy destination views eagerly can slow taps.

cards.title: toolbar
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.toolbar {}` for nav bar actions.
Takeaway: Standard placement.
Trap: Toolbars need a navigation context to appear.

cards.title: sheet
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.sheet(isPresented:)` shows modal UI.
Takeaway: Driven by state.
Trap: Imperative “present” thinking doesn’t map to SwiftUI.

cards.title: alert
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Alerts are state-driven.
Takeaway: Use a Bool or item to control them.
Trap: Multiple booleans for different alerts gets messy—use an enum.

cards.title: ProgressView
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use ProgressView for loading states.
Takeaway: Clear UX.
Trap: Loading without feedback feels like a freeze.

cards.title: SwiftUI Fundamentals — withAnimation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Wrap state changes in `withAnimation`.
Takeaway: Smooth transitions.
Trap: Animations only occur when state actually changes.

cards.title: SwiftUI Fundamentals — .animation(value:)
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.animation(_, value:)` to animate specific state changes.
Takeaway: Controlled animations.
Trap: Global `.animation` without value can cause unexpected animations.

cards.title: transition
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Transition applies when a view is inserted/removed.
Takeaway: Use with `if` blocks.
Trap: Changing opacity alone won’t trigger a transition unless view is removed.

cards.title: ScrollView
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ScrollView is for custom scroll layouts.
Takeaway: Combine with Lazy stacks for performance.
Trap: Don’t nest scroll views unless you understand gesture conflicts.

cards.title: LazyVStack
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Lazy stacks create views on demand.
Takeaway: Better for long lists.
Trap: Lazy is not magic—heavy cells still lag.

cards.title: LazyVGrid
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use LazyVGrid for grids.
Takeaway: Great for galleries.
Trap: Fixed columns can break on different devices.

cards.title: SwiftUI Fundamentals — Adaptive grid
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.adaptive(minimum:)` columns.
Takeaway: Automatically fits columns.
Trap: Too small minimum creates too many columns.

cards.title: SwiftUI Fundamentals — Safe area
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Safe area avoids notches and system UI.
Takeaway: Keep controls visible.
Trap: `.ignoresSafeArea()` can put buttons under the home indicator.

cards.title: ignoresSafeArea for background
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Ignore safe area mainly for backgrounds.
Takeaway: Full-bleed designs.
Trap: Interactive content under system bars is bad UX.

cards.title: Environment basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Environment provides system values (locale, colorScheme, dismiss).
Takeaway: Adapts UI naturally.
Trap: Don’t use environment as a global state dump.

cards.title: Previews
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use previews with sample data.
Takeaway: Faster UI iteration.
Trap: Running real networking in previews is a bad idea.

cards.title: Preview multiple states
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Preview different states (loading/empty/error).
Takeaway: Catch UI gaps early.
Trap: Only previewing “happy path” hides bugs.

cards.title: Extract subviews
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Extract small subviews for readability.
Takeaway: Reuse and clarity.
Trap: Keeping everything in one body makes refactors hard.

cards.title: Avoid heavy work in body
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Move expensive computations out of body.
Takeaway: Smooth UI.
Trap: Computing filters/sorts in body on every render.

cards.title: Use models for UI data
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Drive UI from models/state.
Takeaway: Predictable updates.
Trap: “Manual UI updates” thinking breaks SwiftUI patterns.

cards.title: Hit targets
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tap targets should be comfortably large.
Takeaway: Add padding or contentShape.
Trap: Tiny icons without padding are hard to tap.

cards.title: contentShape
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `contentShape(Rectangle())` expands tappable area.
Takeaway: Better UX.
Trap: Expanding hit areas can interfere with neighboring controls.

cards.title: Accessibility labels
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Provide accessibility labels for icons.
Takeaway: Better VoiceOver support.
Trap: Icon-only buttons without labels are inaccessible.

cards.title: Color scheme testing
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Test light/dark mode.
Takeaway: Use system colors.
Trap: Hardcoded black/white breaks dark mode.

cards.title: Localization mindset
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Plan for localization.
Takeaway: Avoid hard-coded strings everywhere.
Trap: Layout can break with longer translated text.

cards.title: State-driven UI recap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UI changes come from state changes.
Takeaway: Keep a single source of truth.
Trap: Duplicated state leads to inconsistent UI.

cards.title: UIViewRepresentable hint
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: UIKit views can be wrapped with UIViewRepresentable.
Takeaway: Bridge when needed.
Trap: Don’t default to UIKit wrappers for everything.

cards.title: Performance: stable IDs
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Stable IDs are key for list performance.
Takeaway: Smooth diffing.
Trap: Random IDs cause constant view recreation.

cards.title: Avoid AnyView default
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Prefer @ViewBuilder/Group over AnyView.
Takeaway: Keep type information.
Trap: AnyView can hide performance problems.

cards.title: Data flow goal
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Know who owns state and who only observes it.
Takeaway: One source of truth prevents bugs.
Trap: Duplicating the same state in multiple places.

cards.title: @State meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@State` stores local view state.
Takeaway: Changing it re-renders the view.
Trap: Don’t use @State for shared app-wide state.

cards.title: When to use @State
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use @State for simple local values (text, toggles).
Takeaway: UI-local state belongs near the UI.
Trap: Storing complex app data in @State gets messy fast.

cards.title: @Binding meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@Binding` is a reference to state owned elsewhere.
Takeaway: Child views can edit parent state.
Trap: Don’t create bindings without a real source of truth.

cards.title: $ syntax
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `$value` exposes a Binding to a @State.
Takeaway: Needed for TextField/Toggle.
Trap: Passing `value` instead of `$value` breaks updates.

cards.title: Custom Binding
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `Binding(get:set:)` creates a derived binding.
Takeaway: Great for formatting/validation layers.
Trap: If `set` doesn’t write back, the UI won’t update.

cards.title: State hoisting
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Lift state up when multiple children need it.
Takeaway: Keeps state consistent.
Trap: Each child having its own copy leads to desync.

cards.title: Single source of truth
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Keep one owner for each piece of state.
Takeaway: Predictable UI.
Trap: Two sources means conflict and confusion.

cards.title: @StateObject meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@StateObject` creates and owns an ObservableObject.
Takeaway: The object persists across view re-renders.
Trap: Creating a view model with @ObservedObject can recreate it.

cards.title: @ObservedObject meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@ObservedObject` observes an object created elsewhere.
Takeaway: Parent owns, child observes.
Trap: If you create the object in the child, you’ll likely recreate it.

cards.title: @EnvironmentObject meaning
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: EnvironmentObject is shared state injected from above.
Takeaway: Great for app-wide objects.
Trap: Missing injection causes a runtime crash.

cards.title: Injecting EnvironmentObject
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.environmentObject(appState)` on a root view.
Takeaway: Makes it available down the tree.
Trap: Previews also need injection or they crash.

cards.title: @Environment values
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@Environment` reads system-provided values.
Takeaway: locale, colorScheme, dismiss, etc.
Trap: Environment values are not a replacement for app state.

cards.title: State & Data Flow — dismiss
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@Environment(\.dismiss)` closes the current presentation.
Takeaway: Works for sheets and navigation.
Trap: Calling dismiss when nothing is presented does nothing.

cards.title: ObservableObject basics
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: ObservableObject publishes changes to SwiftUI.
Takeaway: Use `@Published` for observable properties.
Trap: Without @Published, UI won’t update.

cards.title: @Published
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@Published` triggers objectWillChange when property changes.
Takeaway: SwiftUI refreshes dependent views.
Trap: Mutating nested reference types may not trigger updates unless property changes.

cards.title: State & Data Flow — @MainActor ViewModel
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mark UI-facing view models as `@MainActor`.
Takeaway: Safe state updates.
Trap: Do heavy work off-main and then hop back to main.

cards.title: Async work in VM
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Start async loading with `Task` and update state on main.
Takeaway: Responsive UI.
Trap: Forgetting cancellation leads to wasted work and stale updates.

cards.title: Task cancellation
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Cancel tasks when view disappears or request becomes irrelevant.
Takeaway: Prevent stale results.
Trap: Old tasks overwriting newer state is a classic bug.

cards.title: View identity matters
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SwiftUI preserves state based on view identity.
Takeaway: Same identity = same state.
Trap: Changing identity resets @State and @StateObject.

cards.title: .id() resets state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.id(value)` changes identity.
Takeaway: Useful for intentional resets.
Trap: Using `.id(UUID())` forces constant resets and poor performance.

cards.title: Conditional views reset state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Removing/adding a view can reset its @State.
Takeaway: Hoist state above conditional boundaries.
Trap: “My text field cleared” often comes from view recreation.

cards.title: Bindings in lists
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `ForEach($items)` to edit list elements.
Takeaway: You get bindings per element.
Trap: Requires stable IDs—don’t use indices as identity.

cards.title: Index binding trap
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Binding by array index breaks when items move.
Takeaway: Prefer binding by ID.
Trap: Deletions shift indices and you edit the wrong item.

cards.title: Derived state
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Compute derived state instead of storing it.
Takeaway: Fewer sync bugs.
Trap: Storing derived values requires manual updates.

cards.title: Validation pattern
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use derived `isValid` to enable/disable actions.
Takeaway: Better UX.
Trap: Running heavy validation in body hurts performance.

cards.title: onChange
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use `.onChange(of:)` to react to state changes.
Takeaway: Keep side effects controlled.
Trap: Updating the same state inside onChange can create loops.

cards.title: onAppear
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use onAppear to start work when a view appears.
Takeaway: Good for initial loads.
Trap: onAppear can run multiple times (especially in lists).

cards.title: .task modifier
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `.task {}` runs async work tied to view lifecycle.
Takeaway: It cancels automatically on disappear.
Trap: It can rerun when view reappears—guard against duplicates.

cards.title: onDisappear cleanup
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use onDisappear for cleanup.
Takeaway: Stop timers, cancel tasks.
Trap: Don’t rely on it for critical saving—use explicit actions.

cards.title: @AppStorage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: `@AppStorage` persists small values in UserDefaults.
Takeaway: Great for settings.
Trap: Don’t store large data or secrets.

cards.title: @SceneStorage
cards.cardDescription:
Rule: SceneStorage restores UI state per scene.
